explanations.needle: VRCSDK build was aborted at the request of the
explanations.title: My Avatar stopped the upload: VRChat already has this thumbnail
explanations.summary: The thumbnail waiting in the VRChat SDK panel is the exact image VRChat already holds for this avatar. VRChat refuses to upload the same file twice (“This file was already uploaded”), but only after the whole build and the avatar upload, so My Avatar stopped the build right away and took the thumbnail out of the upload.
fixes: Click Build & Publish again: the avatar is uploaded and keeps its current thumbnail.
To change the thumbnail, take a new one in My Avatar (or pick another image in the SDK) before uploading.

explanations.needle: VRCSDK build was aborted at the request of the
explanations.title: My Avatar stopped the upload: the blueprint ID isn't yours
explanations.summary: Before building, My Avatar asked Orbiters who published the avatar this blueprint ID points to: another VRChat account did. VRChat would have refused the upload after the whole build, so the build was stopped right away.
fixes: In the window My Avatar opened, click Clear the blueprint ID, then give the avatar a name and a thumbnail in the SDK panel and Build & Publish again.
Without the window: select the avatar root, find the Pipeline Manager component and click Detach.

explanations.needle: VRCSDK build was aborted at the request of the
explanations.title: A tool stopped the build ({callback})
explanations.summary: Before every build, the VRChat SDK asks the tools installed in the project whether the avatar can be built. {callback} said no, so nothing was built or uploaded.
fixes: Look for the tool's own message or window just before this log: it says why.
Fix what it reports, then Build & Publish again.

explanations.needle: [My Avatar] Build & Publish stopped before the build: the blueprint ID
explanations.title: The blueprint ID belongs to someone else's avatar
explanations.summary: The avatar's Pipeline Manager carries the ID of an avatar another VRChat account published, often left in a prefab by its creator. VRChat only lets you update avatars you published, so My Avatar stopped Build & Publish before the build instead of letting it fail after the upload.
fixes: In the window My Avatar opened, click Clear the blueprint ID: the avatar is uploaded as a new one.
Then give it a name and a thumbnail in the VRChat SDK panel and click Build & Publish.

explanations.title: VRCFury is building {avatar}
explanations.summary: VRCFury applies its features (toggles, armature links, full controllers…) when you enter Play Mode, build a test copy or upload. This line marks the start of that build; the lines that follow are its progress. The avatar saved in your scene isn't changed.
fixes: Nothing to do: it only marks the start of VRCFury's build.

explanations.title: VRCFury finished building the avatar
explanations.summary: VRCFury applied all its features without error. Warnings logged during the build still deserve a look.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.needle: VRCFury components not found in avatar. Skipping.
explanations.title: No VRCFury component on this avatar
explanations.summary: VRCFury checks every avatar that is built or enters Play Mode. This one has no VRCFury component, so VRCFury leaves it untouched.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: VRCFury build step ({percent}%)
explanations.summary: VRCFury logs each step of its build; this one is {step}. If a build fails, the last step logged before the error tells which part of VRCFury was running.
fixes: Nothing to do: these lines only show progress.

explanations.title: VRCFury found {feature} on {object}
explanations.summary: Before building, VRCFury collects the features of every VRCFury component on the avatar. Each line names one feature and the object that holds it.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: Armature Link: {bone}
explanations.summary: An Armature Link merges the bones of a prop or piece of clothing into the avatar's armature so it moves with the body. The line names the bone being linked (the Armature Link's 'Link From').
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.needle: Animator Layer Control Offset Builder Report:
explanations.title: VRCFury updated Animator Layer Controls
explanations.summary: Merging controllers moves layers to new positions. VRC Animator Layer Control behaviours point at layers by number, so VRCFury rewrites them to the new numbers. The report lists each change and is empty when there was nothing to update.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: VRCFury changed the icon of '{menu}'
explanations.summary: An Override Menu Icon feature (or SPS Options) replaced the icon of '{menu}' in the avatar's expression menu.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: VRCFury moves the menu '{from}' to '{to}'
explanations.summary: VRCFury moves '{from}' to '{to}' in the expression menu, for a Move or Rename Menu Item feature or for SPS Options. It always tries to move the old 'Holes' and 'Sockets' menus into the SPS menu, so those lines appear even when the avatar has no such menu.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.pattern: ^Largest renderer is (?<renderer>.+?) with linear size of (?<size>[0-9.]+)
explanations.title: Largest renderer: {renderer}
explanations.summary: VRCFury's bounding box fix names the mesh with the biggest bounds (size {size}: half-width + half-height + half-depth, in meters). It then grows the bounds of the other skinned meshes toward it, within the avatar's overall bounds, so small props like hair don't vanish at some camera angles.
fixes: Nothing to do if it's the body or another large mesh.
If it's unexpected (an object far from the avatar, a huge particle mesh), move or remove it: every other mesh's bounds grow toward it.
A name starting with __XRayGizmos_ is the Orbiters Toolkit's armature overlay (the bones drawn over the Scene view), which is left out of builds; if it reached one, update Orbiters Toolkit.

explanations.title: VRCFury's blend tree optimizer report
explanations.summary: VRCFury merges simple toggle layers into a single Direct Blend Tree to use fewer FX layers. The report lists each layer it checked: OPTIMIZED, or Not Optimizing with the reason (a transition with a duration, a weight other than 1, a layer driven by an Animator Layer Control…).
fixes: Nothing to do: layers that aren't optimized keep working as separate layers.
To also optimize layers VRCFury didn't create, add a Direct Tree Optimizer to the avatar.

explanations.title: VRCFury's resting state report
explanations.summary: VRCFury lists the default values it gives properties its features animate (a toggle's off state, a slider's starting value…) and which feature set each. The avatar shows these values until someone uses its menu.
fixes: Nothing to do. If something loads on or off unexpectedly, look it up here to find the feature that set it.

explanations.title: VRCFury's tracking control report
explanations.summary: VRCFury checks whether several features or controllers change Tracking Control (eyes, mouth, hands…) and, if so, merges them so they don't override each other. 'No' and an empty list of contributors mean nothing needed merging.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: The avatar mixes Write Defaults on and off
explanations.summary: Write Defaults should be the same on every state. The states listed after 'Weird states' don't match the rest of the avatar's controllers (Direct Blend Tree states also need it on), which can make animations stick or not reset.
fixes: Choose Auto-Fix when VRCFury asks, or add VRCFury's Fix Write Defaults to the avatar root (Auto): VRCFury then makes every layer consistent.
Or set Write Defaults the same way on the listed states yourself.

explanations.title: VRCFury uses Write Defaults {value}
explanations.summary: Write Defaults must be the same on every state for animations to behave. VRCFury counted how the avatar's states are set (the counts in the message) and uses {value} for the layers it changes ({scope}). 'mode' is the Fix Write Defaults setting, or Disabled when the avatar has none.
fixes: Nothing to do, unless animations don't reset as expected: then add VRCFury's Fix Write Defaults to the avatar (Auto).

explanations.title: VRCFury skipped an upload-only step
explanations.summary: VRCFury also runs avatar build hooks in Play Mode and for test copies. Some hooks are slow and only matter for real uploads, such as Poiyomi's and lilToon's material locking, so VRCFury skipped {plugin} until an actual upload.
fixes: Nothing to do: they run normally when you upload.

explanations.pattern: ^Removing layer (?<layer>.+) from (?<controller>\w+) because it doesn't do anything
explanations.title: Empty layer '{layer}' removed from {controller}
explanations.summary: No animation in this layer changes anything that exists on the avatar, and it has no behaviours, so VRCFury removes it to save performance. Usual for placeholder layers and for layers VRCFury generated ([VF…] names) that ended up unused.
fixes: Nothing to do if '{layer}' is a placeholder or a [VF…] layer.
If '{layer}' should do something, its animations target objects that don't exist: compare their paths with the hierarchy (VRCFury lists the removed properties in another warning).
In Play Mode and test copies VRCFury may keep the layer, renamed '(NO VALID ANIMATIONS)', so you can inspect it.

explanations.needle: properties from animation clips that targeted objects that do not exist
explanations.title: {count} animated properties point to nothing
explanations.summary: Some animations in the avatar's controllers target objects or components that aren't on this avatar: renamed, moved or deleted objects, or clips made for another avatar. VRCFury strips them from the build. Each line gives the path, the property and the clip.
fixes: Nothing to do if those objects were removed on purpose or the clips come from another avatar base.
If something stops animating, find its path in the list and rename the object back or fix the clip.

explanations.needle: because it already ran on that object
explanations.pattern: preventing OnPreprocessAvatar from running on (?<avatar>.+) because
explanations.title: {avatar} was already built in Play Mode
explanations.summary: In Play Mode, something asked to build this avatar again after it was already built (Gesture Manager and Av3Emulator often do). Running the build hooks twice would break it, so VRCFury skips the second run.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.needle: VRCFury is disabling network sync for
explanations.pattern: disabling network sync for (?<param>.+) because it is driven by an AAP
explanations.title: Parameter '{param}' no longer synced
explanations.summary: '{param}' is set by an animation inside the FX controller (an Animated Animator Parameter, AAP). Every player computes it locally, so syncing it would only waste network bits; VRCFury turns its sync off in the build.
fixes: Nothing to do. To silence it, untick Synced for '{param}' in the Expression Parameters.

explanations.needle: as animated since it targets a humanoid bone
explanations.title: PhysBone on {path} marked Is Animated
explanations.summary: A PhysBone whose root is a humanoid bone (the hips for a skirt or tail, for example) stops that bone from ever being animated unless Is Animated is on: sitting, emotes and dances would break. VRCFury turns it on in the build.
fixes: Nothing to do. To silence it, tick Is Animated on that PhysBone yourself.

explanations.title: A VRCFury asset is missing some files
explanations.summary: A Full Controller refers to animations, menus or parameter files that aren't in the project. It allows missing assets, so the build continues, but whatever used those files won't work.
fixes: Import the package the asset came from again, with the packages it depends on.
The message lists the missing files.

explanations.needle: Root bone is null on armature link.
explanations.title: An Armature Link has no bone to link
explanations.summary: An Armature Link has nothing in 'Link From (Prop / Clothing)', so VRCFury skips it: that prop or piece of clothing won't follow the body.
fixes: Select the object with the Armature Link and set 'Link From' to the root bone of the prop or clothing (often its Hips).

explanations.needle: contained a corrupt behaviour. It has been removed.
explanations.title: Broken behaviour removed from {location}
explanations.summary: A state or layer of an animator controller holds a behaviour whose script is missing or damaged. VRCFury removes it from the build so the build can go on; whatever it did (parameter driver, tracking control…) won't happen.
fixes: Open the controller, select the state named in the message and remove the empty or Missing behaviour.
If it should be there, reinstall the tool or VRChat SDK that provides it.

explanations.pattern: ^Clip (?<clip>.+) contains (?:an invalid binding|a binding that is missing a curve)$
explanations.title: A damaged property in an animation clip
explanations.summary: One animated property of the clip {clip} has no path, name, type or curve, so VRCFury ignores it. The rest of the clip still plays.
fixes: Open the clip in the Animation window and delete properties shown as missing, or recreate the clip.

explanations.title: VRCFury's Blendshape Optimizer report
explanations.summary: The Blendshape Optimizer bakes the blendshapes nothing animates into the meshes and removes them, which saves memory. The report lists, mesh by mesh, what it kept and what it baked.
fixes: Nothing to do. If a blendshape a tool changes at runtime disappeared, animate it somewhere or remove the Blendshape Optimizer.

explanations.title: VRCFury note
explanations.summary: VRCFury reports something it did on its own, such as a fix it applies to Unity, the VRChat SDK or another tool while the editor runs.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: VRCFury warning
explanations.summary: VRCFury noticed something it worked around or couldn't apply. The message says what; the avatar usually still builds.
fixes: Read the message for the object or feature it names.
If it mentions an unsupported version or a failed patch, update VRCFury (Tools › VRCFury › Update VRCFury, or the VRChat Creator Companion).

explanations.title: This branch isn't on a remote yet
explanations.summary: Mixer Git asks Git how far the current branch is ahead of or behind its copy on the remote (its upstream). This branch has none yet, so Git answers with an error. Nothing is wrong: there's nothing to compare until you push.
fixes: Nothing to do if you don't use a remote (GitHub, GitLab…).
Otherwise press Push in Mixer Git once: it publishes the branch, links it to the remote, and this message stops.
No remote yet? Connect one in Mixer Git's Settings (Remote › Connect…).

explanations.title: A refresh was replaced by a newer one
explanations.summary: Mixer Git stopped this read because a newer refresh of its window had started; the newer one shows the current state.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.stackNeedle: Command interrupted by editor reload or shutdown.
explanations.title: Git command stopped by a script reload or Unity closing
explanations.summary: Unity reloaded its scripts (after a code change or when entering Play Mode) or was closing while this command ran, so Mixer Git stopped it. Reads are repeated on the next refresh.
fixes: If it was an action you started (commit, push, update…), check Mixer Git's history and run it again if it didn't complete.

explanations.stackNeedle: does not have any commits yet
explanations.title: The repository has no commit yet
explanations.summary: Git can't show history or compare branches before the first commit, so Mixer Git's reads fail until then.
fixes: Make the first commit in Mixer Git and this stops.

explanations.title: The repository has no commit yet
explanations.summary: Mixer Git asked Git for the current commit (HEAD), and there is none: the repository has no commit yet. Mixer Git shows an empty history until the first commit.
fixes: Make the first commit in Mixer Git and this stops.

explanations.title: Git needs you to sign in to the remote
explanations.summary: The remote asked for a user name and password, but Git can't show its sign-in prompt inside Unity. Git needs saved credentials for this server.
fixes: Open a terminal in the project folder and run git fetch: Git for Windows opens a sign-in window (Git Credential Manager) and saves your credentials. Mixer Git then uses them.
For GitHub with GitHub CLI installed, gh auth setup-git also lets Git use your GitHub CLI sign-in.

explanations.title: The remote refused your credentials
explanations.summary: The saved sign-in for this server was rejected: an expired token, a changed password, or an account without access to this repository.
fixes: In Windows Credential Manager › Windows Credentials, remove the entry for the server (for example git:https://github.com), then run git fetch in a terminal in the project folder to sign in again.
Check that the account you sign in with can access the repository.

explanations.title: Your account can't push to this repository
explanations.summary: The server answered 403 (forbidden): the signed-in account can read the repository but not write to it, or its token lacks write permission.
fixes: Sign in with the account that owns the repository or was invited to it with write access.
With a personal access token, give it write access to the repository's contents.

explanations.title: The remote repository wasn't found
explanations.summary: The remote's address points to a repository that doesn't exist, or to a private one the signed-in account can't see.
fixes: Check the remote's address in Mixer Git's Settings (Remote).
Sign in with an account that has access to the repository.

explanations.title: Git couldn't reach the server
explanations.summary: The server's name couldn't be resolved: no internet connection, a DNS problem, or a VPN or proxy in the way.
fixes: Check your connection, then try again.

explanations.title: Push rejected: the remote has newer commits
explanations.summary: The branch on the remote has commits you don't have yet (pushed from another computer or made on the website). Git never overwrites them.
fixes: Press Update (pull) in Mixer Git, then push again.
If Update says it can't fast-forward, both sides have new commits: merge the remote branch into yours first.

explanations.title: Update stopped: the branches have diverged
explanations.summary: Mixer Git's Update only fast-forwards and never creates a merge on its own. Your branch and the remote branch both have new commits.
fixes: In Mixer Git's branch list, right-click the remote branch (origin/…) and merge it into your branch.
Resolve conflicts if Mixer Git shows any, then push.

explanations.title: Another Git program is using the repository
explanations.summary: Git found an index.lock file: another Git program is working in this project (a terminal, a code editor, GitHub Desktop…), or one crashed and left its lock behind. Mixer Git waits and retries a few times before giving up.
fixes: Wait for the other Git program to finish, then try again.
If no Git program is running, delete the file .git/index.lock in the project folder.

explanations.title: Git doesn't trust the project folder
explanations.summary: The project folder belongs to another Windows user (common on external or second drives, or with a project copied from another PC), so Git refuses to work in it.
fixes: Run the command Git prints in the output once (git config --global --add safe.directory followed by the project folder), then refresh Mixer Git.

explanations.title: Merge conflicts to resolve
explanations.summary: The merge (or cherry-pick, revert, rebase) stopped because the same parts of some files changed on both sides. Git marked those files as conflicted and waits for you.
fixes: Open Mixer Git's Conflicts tab, choose a version for each file, then press Finish merge (or Continue).
To go back to how things were, press Cancel merge (or Cancel) in the same tab.

explanations.title: Uncommitted changes are in the way
explanations.summary: Switching branches, updating or merging would overwrite files you changed and haven't committed, so Git stopped before touching anything.
fixes: Commit your changes, or put them on Mixer Git's Shelf, then try again.

explanations.title: GitHub refused files over 100 MB
explanations.summary: GitHub rejects any pushed file larger than 100 MB, so nothing was pushed. The output names the files.
fixes: Track such files with Git LFS, or keep them out of the repository (.gitignore).
They're already in commits: take them out of the commits that added them (amend or reset those commits), then push again.

explanations.title: The connection broke during the transfer
explanations.summary: The transfer to or from the server was cut: a push too big for the server (HTTP 413), an unstable connection, or a proxy or antivirus closing it.
fixes: Push fewer or smaller commits at a time; keep big binaries in Git LFS.
For HTTP 413 or send failures, run git config --global http.postBuffer 524288000 in a terminal, then try again.

explanations.stackNeedle: Please tell me who you are
explanations.title: Git doesn't know your name and e-mail
explanations.summary: Every commit records an author, and no name or e-mail is set for Git on this computer, so the commit failed.
fixes: In a terminal, run git config --global user.name "Your Name" and git config --global user.email "you@example.com", then commit again.

explanations.title: A file is locked by another program
explanations.summary: Git couldn't replace a file because a program has it open. On Windows, Unity keeps plugin DLLs and some assets locked while it runs.
fixes: Close the program that holds the file and try again.
For files Unity locks (DLLs), close Unity, run the action from a terminal or another Git tool, then reopen Unity.

explanations.title: Part of the Git history is damaged
explanations.summary: Git found a damaged object in the repository, usually after a crash or power loss while Git was writing, or a sync tool changing the .git folder.
fixes: Stop committing for now so nothing gets worse.
In Mixer Git's Backups tab, Restore… recreates the project from a backup in a new folder. Or clone the repository again from the remote. Then copy your uncommitted work into the new copy.
Keep the project's .git folder out of OneDrive, Dropbox and other sync tools.

explanations.title: GitHub CLI isn't signed in
explanations.summary: Mixer Git uses GitHub CLI (gh) to create and connect GitHub repositories, and gh has no signed-in account.
fixes: Sign in from Mixer Git's Settings (Remote › GitHub / GitLab…), or run gh auth login in a terminal.

explanations.title: Git answered 'no': not an error
explanations.summary: Some Git commands answer a yes/no question with their exit code: diff --quiet exits with 1 when there are changes, check-ignore when no file is ignored, config --get when the setting isn't set, symbolic-ref --quiet when no branch is checked out, rev-parse --verify --quiet when the revision doesn't exist. Mixer Git reads that answer; nothing failed.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: Git command run by Mixer Git
explanations.summary: The Mixer console lists every Git command Mixer Git runs (refreshing its window, reading history, staging, committing…) with how long it took; they don't appear in Unity's Console. 'ok' means Git succeeded; what Git printed is under the message.
fixes: Nothing to do. Filter out the Mixer Git source if these lines get in the way.

explanations.title: Git returned an error
explanations.summary: Mixer Git ran this Git command and Git stopped with an error (the number after 'exit' is Git's exit code). Git's own reason is in the output, under 'stderr'.
fixes: Read the stderr lines in the output: Git says what went wrong.
Failed background refreshes are tried again on the next refresh. Actions you started (commit, push, update…) can be run again from Mixer Git once the cause is fixed.
To dig deeper, run the same command in a terminal opened in the project folder.

explanations.title: A Git command took too long and was stopped
explanations.summary: Mixer Git waits 30 seconds for quick commands and 15 minutes for long ones (commit, push, update, fetch, backups), then stops Git. The operation may not have finished.
fixes: Look for a Git sign-in window hidden behind Unity: Git waits for it.
Antivirus scans and cloud sync (OneDrive, Dropbox) of the project folder slow Git down a lot: exclude the project folder.
Very large files make Git slow: keep big binaries in Git LFS or out of the repository.
Then run the action again from Mixer Git.

explanations.needle: [Mixer Git] Creating VRChat avatar upload commit for
explanations.title: Mixer Git is recording the avatar upload
explanations.summary: After a successful VRChat upload, Mixer Git commits the project as it was uploaded, so you can go back to that exact version later.
fixes: Nothing to do. You can turn it off in Mixer Git's Settings (Commit after each upload).

explanations.needle: [Mixer Git] Created VRChat avatar upload commit
explanations.title: Avatar upload recorded in Git
explanations.summary: Mixer Git committed the project as it was when the avatar was uploaded. The commit appears in Mixer Git's log, with a row naming the upload if that setting is on.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.needle: [Mixer Git] VRChat avatar upload commit skipped by Mixer Git settings.
explanations.title: Avatar upload not recorded (setting off)
explanations.summary: Commit after each upload is off in Mixer Git's Settings, so this upload made no commit.
fixes: Nothing to do. Turn the setting on if you want every upload recorded.

explanations.needle: [Mixer Git] Could not prepare VRChat avatar upload commit:
explanations.title: The avatar upload couldn't be recorded in Git
explanations.summary: The upload itself worked, but Mixer Git couldn't save the open scenes and assets before committing ({reason}), so it made no commit.
fixes: Save the scene (File › Save), then commit from Mixer Git so this version is recorded.

explanations.title: Mixer Git couldn't record the avatar upload
explanations.summary: The VRChat upload finished, but Mixer Git's automatic commit of it failed. The message gives the reason.
fixes: Fix what the message says, then commit from Mixer Git so this upload's version is recorded.

explanations.title: Mixer Git's automatic backup failed
explanations.summary: Once a day, Mixer Git saves a copy of the whole Git history (by default in Documents › Mixer Git Backups). This one failed; the project and its history are unchanged, only the extra copy is missing.
fixes: Check that the backup folder exists and has free space (Mixer Git's Backups tab shows it; Open goes there).
Press Back up now in the Backups tab to try again and see the full error.

explanations.title: AI assistant bridge disconnected
explanations.summary: MCP for Unity's connection to its server closed: the server stopped or restarted, the computer slept, or Unity was busy for a long time (importing, compiling, running tests) and the server dropped the session. MCP for Unity reconnects by itself; only the AI assistant's access to Unity is affected.
fixes: Nothing to do if the assistant works again a moment later.
If the assistant doesn't recover, open Window › MCP for Unity › Toggle MCP Window, start the server if it's stopped (Start Server), then start the session again (Start Session or Connect).
A request sent while the connection was down may have failed: ask the assistant to check its result.

explanations.title: AI assistant bridge: keep-alive failed
explanations.summary: MCP for Unity regularly pings its local server to keep the connection open. The ping failed, so it treats the connection as closed and reconnects; a 'Connection closed' warning usually follows.
fixes: Nothing to do if the assistant works again a moment later.
If the assistant doesn't recover, open Window › MCP for Unity › Toggle MCP Window, start the server if it's stopped (Start Server), then start the session again (Start Session or Connect).

explanations.title: AI assistant bridge: connection lost
explanations.summary: The connection to MCP for Unity's local server broke while Unity was waiting for the assistant's next request. MCP for Unity reconnects by itself.
fixes: Nothing to do if the assistant works again a moment later.
If the assistant doesn't recover, open Window › MCP for Unity › Toggle MCP Window, start the server if it's stopped (Start Server), then start the session again (Start Session or Connect).

explanations.needle: MCP-FOR-UNITY: [WebSocket] Unexpected receive error: WebSocket is not
explanations.title: An AI assistant request finished after a disconnect
explanations.summary: Unity finished a request from the AI assistant, but the connection had already closed, so the answer couldn't be sent back. The assistant may report that request as failed or timed out even though Unity did the work.
fixes: Ask the assistant to check whether the change was made before it tries again.

explanations.title: AI assistant bridge can't reach its server
explanations.summary: MCP for Unity has failed to reconnect to its local server for about a minute. It keeps retrying every 30 seconds.
fixes: Start the server from Window › MCP for Unity › Toggle MCP Window (Start Server), or restart your AI client.
Ignore it if you're not using the assistant right now.

explanations.title: AI assistant bridge couldn't connect
explanations.summary: MCP for Unity couldn't open a connection to its server: the server isn't running, its address or port is wrong, or a required API key is missing.
fixes: Open Window › MCP for Unity › Toggle MCP Window, start the server (Start Server) and check the server URL.
For a remote server, check its address and API key.

explanations.needle: MCP-FOR-UNITY: Local HTTP server did not become reachable
explanations.title: MCP for Unity's local server didn't start
explanations.summary: MCP for Unity launched its local server but it never answered. The end of the server's launch log is in the message: often a missing dependency (uv or Python), no internet on the first launch, or the port already used by another program.
fixes: Read the launch log lines in the message.
Run the command the message gives in a terminal to see the full error.

explanations.title: MCP for Unity is starting its local server
explanations.summary: The server that connects AI assistants (Claude, Cursor…) to Unity is starting. The first launch can take a minute while it installs what it needs.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: MCP for Unity's server is ready
explanations.summary: The local server answers; MCP for Unity now connects Unity to it.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: AI assistant bridge connected
explanations.summary: Unity is connected to MCP for Unity's server: AI assistants can now read and change the project through it.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: MCP for Unity updated AI client settings
explanations.summary: Once per editor session, MCP for Unity updates the MCP settings of the AI clients installed on this computer (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code…) so they point to the installed version of the package.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: Editor throttling changed for a test run
explanations.summary: While tests run, MCP for Unity sets Unity's Interaction Mode to No Throttling so the tests keep running when Unity is in the background, then restores your setting when they finish.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: MCP for Unity note
explanations.summary: MCP for Unity, the bridge that lets AI assistants control the editor, reports what it's doing. Nothing here changes your project by itself.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: MCP for Unity reported a problem
explanations.summary: MCP for Unity, the bridge that lets AI assistants control the editor, couldn't complete something: a connection, a setting or a request from the assistant. Only what the assistant was doing is affected.
fixes: If the assistant was making a change, ask it to check the result.
If it keeps happening, start the session again from Window › MCP for Unity › Toggle MCP Window.

explanations.needle: had become dangling during an undo operation
explanations.pattern: ^Component of type (?<type>\S+) was added to (?<object>.+) using GameObject\.AddComponent\(\)
explanations.title: A component added without Undo was lost in an undo
explanations.summary: A script added a component ({type}) to '{object}' outside Unity's undo system. An undo (yours, or one a tool ran) then rewound that object and left the component orphaned, so Unity cleaned it up.
fixes: Check '{object}': if it lost a component it needs, run the tool's action again.
If a tool causes it repeatedly, tell its author: components must be added with Undo.AddComponent.

explanations.pattern: Build asset version error: (?<path>\S+) in SourceAssetDB has modification time
explanations.title: A file changed while Unity imported it
explanations.summary: '{path}' was saved again (by a code editor, Git, a sync tool or another program) while Unity was importing it, so its recorded and actual modification times differ. Unity imports it again on the next refresh.
fixes: Nothing to do if it doesn't come back.
If it repeats for the same file, something keeps rewriting it (cloud sync, antivirus, a running tool): pause it or exclude the project folder, then right-click the file › Reimport.

explanations.title: Stylesheet uses an unsupported property
explanations.summary: The UI stylesheet {file} (line {line}) uses '{property}', which Unity's UI Toolkit doesn't support (USS is only part of CSS). Unity ignores that line; the window using the stylesheet works the same.
fixes: Nothing to do: the author of the tool the file belongs to (see its path) should remove or rename the property.

explanations.title: A tool's stylesheet has a {kind}
explanations.summary: Unity found something it can't read in the UI stylesheet {file} (line {line}) while importing it. Only how that tool's window looks can be affected.
fixes: Nothing to do on your side: the tool's author should fix the stylesheet. Updating the tool may already include a fix.

explanations.title: VRChat SDK reused {count} network IDs
explanations.summary: While building '{avatar}', the SDK keeps the network IDs already stored on the avatar for synced components such as PhysBones and gives new ones to the rest. It logs this count as a warning on every build; 0 is common (first builds, test copies, IDs never saved on the avatar).
fixes: Nothing to do.

If you upload PC and Android versions of the same avatar, keep their IDs the same: export them from one and import them into the other with VRChat SDK › Utilities › Network ID Import and Export Utility.

explanations.title: The avatar's network IDs conflict
explanations.summary: The SDK stops the build when two synced components (PhysBones…) share a network ID or an ID is out of range, usually after copying parts between avatars or editing IDs by hand.
fixes: Open VRChat SDK › Utilities › Network ID Import and Export Utility, choose the avatar as Target and press Scan For Conflicts.
Fix what it lists, or press Clear Scene IDs so the next build assigns new IDs (export them again to the avatar's other-platform version if you have one).
Then build again.

explanations.title: Anchor Override of {renderer} set to {anchor}
explanations.summary: During the build, Poiyomi's auto anchor gives every mesh without an Anchor Override the same anchor (the {anchor} bone), so all parts of the avatar get the same lighting in VRChat instead of mismatched or flickering light. It changes the avatar being built, not the one saved in your scene.
fixes: Nothing to do. To turn it off, untick 'Auto set Anchor Overrides' in Thry › ThryEditor › Settings, or add an empty object named AutoAnchorDisabled to the avatar.

explanations.title: ReFit linked refitted clothing to the body
explanations.summary: During the build, ReFit makes the blendshapes it generated on refitted clothing follow the body: it copies the body's current blendshape weights and, where an animation drives a body blendshape, animates the clothing's matching shape the same way. The numbers say how much it linked.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.needle: was removed during the build (a mesh or blendshape optimizer?)
explanations.pattern: blendshape '(?<shape>[^']+)' of (?<mesh>.+?) was removed during the build \(a mesh or blendshape optimizer\?\) while the body's '(?<source>[^']+)' is animated
explanations.title: Build removed refitted blendshape '{shape}'
explanations.summary: Another build step, usually a mesh or blendshape optimizer, removed '{shape}' from {mesh} while the body's '{source}' is animated. That part of the clothing won't follow the body when '{source}' changes. The upload goes on.
fixes: Set the optimizer to keep the refitted mesh's blendshapes, or leave that mesh out of blendshape optimization.
Build again and check the warning is gone.

explanations.needle: the body a refitted mesh was made for was removed during the build
explanations.title: The body of refitted clothing was removed by the build
explanations.summary: A build step removed or merged the body mesh that ReFit fitted clothing to, so the clothing's blendshapes can't follow the body's animations. The upload goes on.
fixes: Find the tool that merges or removes meshes during the build (a mesh merger or optimizer) and leave the body out of it.

explanations.needle: was refitted for a body that is not part of
explanations.pattern: ^\[Orbiters\] (?<mesh>.+) was refitted for a body that is not part of (?<avatar>.+?):
explanations.title: {mesh} was refitted for another body
explanations.summary: {mesh} was fitted to a body mesh that isn't inside {avatar} (clothing moved from another avatar, for example), so its blendshapes won't follow this avatar's animations.
fixes: Refit the clothing again with ReFit, on this avatar's body.

explanations.needle: does not follow the body: its renderer is animated.
explanations.title: {renderer} won't follow the body
explanations.summary: Follow body blendshapes rebuilds static meshes during the build so they follow the body's blendshapes, but {renderer} is animated (a toggle or material swap), and rebuilding it would break that animation. It's left as is.
fixes: Toggle a parent object instead of {renderer} itself, or take it out of Follow body blendshapes.

explanations.title: ReFit: {body} shrinks under {clothing} in the upload
explanations.summary: When {clothing} was fitted, ReFit noted the {count} vertices of {body} that would show through it and how far to pull them in. The upload gets that as a blendshape of {body} that follows the clothing: on while it shows, off while it is hidden, toggles included ({how}). Only the build copy changes.
fixes: Nothing to do.
If the body shows through or looks dented, fit the clothing again with ReFit (its record keeps the shrink), or turn the body shrink off in the fit's options.

explanations.pattern: ^\[Orbiters\] ReFit: (?<clothing>.+?) offers (?<count>\d+) fits in the menu \((?<menu>.+)\)\.
explanations.title: ReFit: {clothing} gets {count} fits in the menu
explanations.summary: The fits kept for {clothing} (Keep this fit in ReFit) become blendshapes of its mesh in the upload, and a menu at {menu} switches between them in the game, one at a time; the fit worn in the scene is the one on at first.
fixes: Nothing to do.
To have fewer choices, remove kept fits in ReFit's record of the clothing.

explanations.needle: refit cache entries (or folders) no engine finds any more.
explanations.title: Old ReFit cache entries were removed
explanations.summary: ReFit keeps the meshes it fitted under Assets/Orbiters/ReFit/Cache, one folder per engine version. After an update, the entries of older versions (and of the cache's former layout) are removed once the new version stores or reads a result, since no engine reads them any more. The fitted meshes your avatars use stay.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: Orbiters Toolkit's {suite} tests passed
explanations.summary: The avatar gizmos' (bones, weight paint, mesh edges) self-tests ran from the Test Runner and passed.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: Mixer console performance test result
explanations.summary: Printed by the Mixer console's own automated tests: how long it took to take in, filter and search a million generated logs. It only appears when someone runs the Mixer console's tests.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: The Mixer console hit an internal error
explanations.summary: The Mixer console's capture or window refresh failed. It keeps running and reports this at most every 10 seconds; some logs may be missing from its list meanwhile. Unity's Console still has everything.
fixes: Close and reopen the Mixer console window.
If it repeats, report it to the Mixer console's author with this log and its stack trace.

explanations.title: '{member}' hides an inherited member
explanations.summary: A class declares '{member}' with the same name as '{inherited}' of its base class. The code compiles and works; the compiler only asks the author to state that hiding it is intended.
fixes: Nothing to do unless you wrote this code: then add the new keyword (or override, if the base member is virtual).

explanations.title: Expected warning from an MCB health check
explanations.summary: MCB's health checks apply small test meshes built from temporary files outside your project. Their original model can't be loaded from there, so MCB poses the test avatar with the bone positions stored in the test payload, which is what the check expects. Your avatar isn't touched.
fixes: Nothing to do. The health check's own result (its dialog, or the status under Health Checks in Advanced Options) tells whether it passed.

explanations.title: Expected warning from an MCB health check
explanations.summary: The Native Mesh Payload health check renames a bone of its test model on purpose ('MissingHips'), to prove that MCB then leaves the test mesh untouched instead of restoring it with the wrong bones. Your avatar isn't touched.
fixes: Nothing to do. The health check's own result tells whether it passed.

explanations.title: Expected message from an MCB health check
explanations.summary: The Version Apply/Reset health check backs up and restores a temporary test FBX, outside your project, to verify that MCB never loses an original model. Your avatar's files aren't touched.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: A twisting bone's weights couldn't be written
explanations.summary: While the avatar builds (upload or Play Mode), MCB adds the version's twisting bones, for example on the forearms, and spreads each mesh's skin weights between the bone and its new twist bone. Unity refused to store the new weights in that mesh's vertex format. The build goes on, but on that mesh a twist may be missing: the limb twists as on the original base, or pinches.
fixes: Enter Play Mode (or use Gesture Manager), turn each wrist and compare both forearms.
If one of them pinches or doesn't twist, report it to the MCB developer with this stack trace and the version name.
Update MCB through the VRChat Creator Companion when a newer release is out: the twist is built by MCB, not by your project.

explanations.pattern: Main Object Name '(?<name>[^']*)' does not match filename '(?<file>[^']*)'
explanations.title: Unity notes the name of a cached mesh file
explanations.summary: MCB stores a version's decoded meshes as a cache asset under Assets/MCB/generated/advancedMeshPayloads, named after the FBX they come from ('{file}'). The name keeps the FBX's '.fbx' part, and Unity expects the asset inside to carry exactly the file's name, so it warns. The cached meshes load and work normally.
fixes: Nothing to do. Advanced Options › Generated Advanced Meshes › Delete unused generated meshes clears caches no version uses anymore.

explanations.needle: Non-secure network connections disabled in Player Settings
explanations.title: The connectivity report's plain-HTTP check was blocked
explanations.summary: When a request to the Orbiters server fails, and when you run Connectivity Tests, MCB builds a connectivity report. One of its checks opens a public test site that only uses plain HTTP, to tell a blocked network from a broken HTTPS connection. This project doesn't allow plain HTTP, so Unity blocked that one check and the report marks it FAIL. MCB itself talks to the Orbiters server over HTTPS.
fixes: Nothing to do for this line.
If MCB shows a connection problem, read the rest of the report in the MCB inspector (or Tools › My Custom Base (MCB) › Connectivity Tests): the other checks tell where the connection stops.

explanations.title: Logged by MCB's automated tests
explanations.summary: An automated test builds a small avatar on purpose without an FX controller. This line is part of the test, not of your avatar.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.needle: Choose a scene MyCustomBase with the Ultirex applied
explanations.title: Ultirex validation started on the wrong object
explanations.summary: The Ultirex validation script (an authoring check under Assets/MCB/Authoring) was given an object that isn't a My Custom Base in an open scene with the Ultirex applied: a wrong or outdated instance ID, an avatar reset to its original base, or a scene that was closed or reloaded since. The check stopped before building anything; your avatar wasn't changed.
fixes: Apply the Ultirex to the avatar with My Custom Base in the open scene, if it isn't applied.
Run the validation again with the instance ID of that avatar's My Custom Base component: instance IDs change when a scene is reloaded.

explanations.title: Custom bases couldn't be listed: no answer from the server
explanations.summary: MCB asks the Orbiters server which custom bases fit your avatar. This request got no answer at all (HTTP 0): you are offline, a firewall, VPN or antivirus blocked Unity, or the server was down or restarting. With Dev Environment ticked in Advanced Options, MCB asks a local development server instead, which then has to be running.
fixes: Check your internet connection, then click Retry under Available Custom Bases in the MCB inspector.
If it keeps failing, open Tools › My Custom Base (MCB) › Connectivity Tests to see where the connection stops.
Untick Dev Environment in Advanced Options unless you run a local Orbiters server.

explanations.title: The server refused the custom base list (HTTP {code})
explanations.summary: MCB asked the Orbiters server which custom bases fit your avatar and got an error back. 401 or 403 mean your session expired or your account can't see these assets; 500 and above is a problem on the server's side. The server's own explanation, if any, follows body= in the message.
fixes: Click Retry under Available Custom Bases in the MCB inspector.
For 401 or 403, connect your Orbiters account again in the MCB inspector.
For 500 and above, wait a few minutes and retry.

explanations.pattern: ^\[(?:NetworkService\] FetchVersionsAsync failed|VersionActions\] Version fetch failed|MCBEditor\] Version fetch error)
explanations.title: The version list couldn't be loaded
explanations.summary: MCB couldn't get the versions of the selected custom base from the Orbiters server: no connection, an expired session or a server error. The message includes the HTTP status and, when there is one, the server's answer. Your avatar and the version applied on it don't change.
fixes: Check your connection, then click Reload versions and banners in Advanced Options (or select the custom base again).
If the message mentions 401 or Unauthorized, connect your Orbiters account again in the MCB inspector.
If it keeps failing, open Tools › My Custom Base (MCB) › Connectivity Tests.

explanations.title: Your account can't access this custom base's versions
explanations.summary: The Orbiters server answered that the connected account doesn't own this custom base, or lacks the role its creator requires, so it sent no versions.
fixes: Check you are signed in with the account that bought or was given the custom base.
Get the custom base from its Orbiters page, or ask its creator for access, then reload the versions.

explanations.title: MCB isn't connected to your Orbiters account
explanations.summary: MCB has no Orbiters sign-in stored, so it can't list custom bases, versions or downloads. With Dev Environment ticked in Advanced Options, the development server needs its own sign-in.
fixes: In the MCB inspector, click Login with Discord or Login with Telegram and finish in your browser.

explanations.needle: [NativeMeshPayload] Could not resolve source pose root
explanations.pattern: Could not resolve source pose root '(?<path>[^']*)'
explanations.title: The version's original model wasn't found in the project
explanations.summary: The version's meshes were made against the original base model at '{path}'. MCB can't load that model in this project (it was moved, renamed or never imported), so it posed the skeleton with the bone positions stored in the version. The result is usually the same; it can differ if your original model was edited.
fixes: If the avatar looks right, nothing to do.
Otherwise import the original base package again so its model is back at that path, then click Reset to Original Avatar and apply the version again.

explanations.needle: [NativeMeshPayload] Could not resolve authoring base transform
explanations.title: '{path}' kept its current position
explanations.summary: To pose the avatar like the version's creator, MCB needs each object's position in the original model or in the version's data. It found neither for '{path}', so it left that object where it is. It usually follows the warning about the original model not being found; mesh objects such as Body or Hair usually don't move anyway.
fixes: Nothing to do if the avatar looks right.
Otherwise fix the warning about the original model logged just before, then apply the version again.

explanations.needle: [NativeMeshPayload] Could not resolve authoring pose transform
explanations.title: The avatar has no '{path}'
explanations.summary: The version poses an object at '{path}' (a path from the avatar root), but MCB found no object there, nor a single object with that name: it was renamed, moved or deleted, or a merged clothing armature reuses the name. MCB skipped it, so that part keeps its current pose.
fixes: Rename or move the object back so it matches '{path}', then click Reset to Original Avatar and apply the version again.
If another tool changed the armature, apply the version on an unchanged avatar first.

explanations.needle: The original base pose could not be kept
explanations.title: The avatar keeps the version's own rest pose
explanations.summary: For versions that aren't encrypted, MCB turns the arms, legs and fingers to point like your original base model (a T-pose, for example). It couldn't: the original model wasn't found, or it or the avatar isn't set up as a Humanoid. The avatar keeps the rest pose of the version's model.
fixes: Check the original base FBX is in the project and its Rig tab says Animation Type: Humanoid (select the FBX, change it if needed and click Apply).
Then click Reset to Original Avatar and apply the version again.

explanations.title: A mesh wasn't restored from the original FBX
explanations.summary: To reset to the original avatar or switch versions, MCB puts each mesh back with the bones of the original FBX. A bone, renderer or bind pose it needs doesn't match your avatar (renamed, deleted, or moved by another tool), so MCB changed none of the meshes of that FBX rather than risk breaking them.
fixes: Read the names in the message: rename or move that bone or object back to where the original model has it.
Then click Reset to Original Avatar again.
If the armature was changed on purpose, restore the avatar from a backup or Mixer Git first.

explanations.title: Corrective layer '{layer}' can't reach the FX controller
explanations.summary: At build, corrective links rewrote layer '{layer}' of a controller that isn't the avatar's FX. VRChat only plays blendshape animations from FX, so MCB copies such layers there, but this build has no FX controller to copy into. That corrective won't play in VRChat.
fixes: Select the avatar and check that VRC Avatar Descriptor › Playable Layers has an FX controller (click Customize to assign one).
Then upload or enter Play Mode again.

explanations.title: Custom veins don't support the shader '{shader}'
explanations.summary: Custom veins are added as a detail normal map, which MCB can set on Poiyomi, Mochie, VRChat and Unity Standard materials only. This material keeps its look, without veins.
fixes: Use a supported shader (Poiyomi, for example) on the body materials if you want the veins, then apply the version again.
Otherwise ignore it: only the veins are missing.

explanations.needle: unused blendshapes left the custom base's meshes
explanations.pattern: (?<removed>\d+) unused blendshapes left the custom base's meshes \((?<renderers>\d+) renderers\)
explanations.title: {removed} unused blendshapes left out of the upload
explanations.summary: When you upload, MCB removes from the custom base's meshes ({renderers} here) the blendshapes that no animation, viseme, eyelid setting or MMD dance uses, and bakes in those held at a fixed value. It keeps the avatar under VRChat's size limits. Only the uploaded copy changes: your scene and Play Mode keep every shape.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: {count} refitted accessories went back to their original mesh
explanations.summary: When you reset to the original avatar or switch versions, MCB puts the clothing and accessories that ReFit adapted to the custom base back on their original meshes. The fits saved for a version come back when that version is applied again.
fixes: Nothing to do. Refit an accessory again if the new version needs it.

explanations.pattern: ^\[MCB\] (?:Version BlendShape links|Manual BlendShape links|Bone animation offset fix) skipped: (?:No version BlendShape links are active|No BlendShape factor link configuration|No applied version|No moved bones|No animation clips with local-position curves|No matching blendshape curves)
explanations.title: Nothing of this kind to add to the build
explanations.summary: Before an upload or Play Mode, MCB adds the applied version's corrective links, the manual links set up in Advanced Options › BlendShape Link Factor Test, and fixes for animations on bones a version moved. This avatar has nothing of that kind, so the step was skipped.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.pattern: ^\[MCB\] (?:Version BlendShape links|Manual BlendShape links|Bone animation offset fix) skipped: (?<reason>.+)
explanations.title: MCB skipped a build step
explanations.summary: Before an upload or Play Mode, MCB adds the applied version's corrective links, your manual links and fixes for animations on bones a version moved. This step didn't run: {reason} When the reason is a missing VRCFury or build controller, the version's correctives won't play in VRChat.
fixes: If the reason mentions VRCFury or a build controller, install VRCFury through the VRChat Creator Companion and keep its components on the avatar, then build again.
Otherwise nothing to do.

explanations.title: Corrective links are being added to the build
explanations.summary: While an avatar builds (upload, Play Mode or a test), MCB and Orbiters Toolkit rewrite the build copies of its animator controllers so correctives and refitted clothing follow the blendshapes that drive them. These lines trace that work. Masks are cleared on the build copy only, so FX can play the blendshape curves; your own controllers aren't changed. ReFit and My Avatar builds log these lines with the [MCB] label too.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: MCB checks your Orbiters account
explanations.summary: Each time an MCB inspector opens (when you select the avatar, after a script reload, or when MCB opens one in the background), MCB asks the Orbiters server whether your account is connected and what it can access.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: Your FBX matches none of the known versions
explanations.summary: MCB recognizes an applied version by the fingerprint (hash) of your avatar's FBX. This one matches none of the versions known for the selected custom base, so MCB shows the avatar as on its original base. That is expected when nothing is applied.
fixes: Nothing to do if your avatar is on its original base.
If a version should be applied, open Advanced Options, click Recalculate current FBX hash, then Reload versions and banners.
If MCB still shows the original base, something changed the FBX outside MCB (a reimport, another tool, a Git checkout): apply the version again.

explanations.needle: [VersionActions] Version fetch skipped because no asset is selected
explanations.title: No custom base selected, so no versions were loaded
explanations.summary: MCB lists the versions of the custom base selected in its gallery. None is selected, so there was nothing to load.
fixes: Pick a custom base under Available Custom Bases in the MCB inspector to see its versions.

explanations.title: MCB starts loading the version list
explanations.summary: Logged each time MCB refreshes the versions of the selected custom base: it reads your FBX's hash, then asks the Orbiters server for the versions that fit it. Despite its wording, 'ApplyOrResetCoroutine completed' doesn't mean a version was applied or reset.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.pattern: ^\[VersionActions\] (?:UpdateAppliedVersionAndState|Inferred native mesh applied version|Keeping applied native mesh version|Deferring state detection|Matched applied version)
explanations.title: MCB checks which version your avatar has
explanations.summary: MCB works out which version is applied from your FBX's hash, the version it recorded on the avatar and the meshes it generated. It does this whenever an MCB inspector opens or the version list refreshes, so these lines repeat a lot.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: Save the scene to keep the version change
explanations.summary: After applying a version with native meshes, MCB doesn't save the project itself, so that Unity doesn't freeze. The scene is marked as changed instead.
fixes: Save the scene (Ctrl+S) once you are happy with the result.

explanations.title: Reset without a confirmation dialog
explanations.summary: The applied version only swaps meshes, so going back to the original avatar doesn't reimport the FBX. MCB skips the confirmation dialog for this quick reset.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: Pick a version in the list
explanations.summary: The Orbiters server didn't mark a recommended version of this custom base for your avatar, so MCB can't preselect one.
fixes: Click a version in the version list of the MCB inspector, then the Apply (or Download version) button.

explanations.title: MCB saved a copy of your original FBX
explanations.summary: Before a version changes your avatar's FBX, MCB copies the original next to it as <name>.fbx.originalbase. Reset to Original Avatar copies it back, and versions are patched against it. MCB never overwrites this copy.
fixes: Keep the .originalbase files: without them MCB can't reset your avatar or switch versions.

explanations.pattern: A Blender export for (?<base>.+?) is waiting
explanations.title: A Blender export for {base} is waiting
explanations.summary: Blender sent changes through Magic Sync, but the avatar connected to that Blender session is in a scene that isn't open. MCB keeps the export until you open it.
fixes: Open the scene with the avatar you clicked Modify with Blender on: MCB applies the export then.

explanations.title: Timing of a native mesh step
explanations.summary: Versions with native meshes ship them as a compressed, often encrypted payload. MCB decodes it into a cache under Assets/MCB/generated/advancedMeshPayloads, reads it, and puts the meshes and bone poses on your avatar. These lines time each step in milliseconds. Versions named nativeMeshHealthCheck, delivery-…, reuse-… or plain-… are MCB's health checks.
fixes: Nothing to do. These timing lines are always logged (Log in Console doesn't hide them): select one and press Delete (Hide messages like this) to hide them here.

explanations.title: Timing of a version apply or reset
explanations.summary: When you apply or reset a version with native meshes, MCB times each step (restoring the original model's state, patches and imports, pose, materials, blendshapes, saving the applied state, hashing the FBX) and prints the milliseconds.
fixes: Nothing to do. These timing lines are always logged (Log in Console doesn't hide them): select one and press Delete (Hide messages like this) to hide them here.

explanations.title: Timing of the dynamic normals bake
explanations.summary: Building a version with dynamic normals, MCB recalculates the lighting normals of the muscle and flex blendshapes, so shading follows the deformation, and bakes them into the version's mesh data. This line times it for one mesh.
fixes: Nothing to do. These timing lines are always logged (Log in Console doesn't hide them): select one and press Delete (Hide messages like this) to hide them here.

explanations.title: Timing of a version build
explanations.summary: When you click Build Version in the creator panel, MCB times each phase (hashing the inputs, packaging the model and logic, metadata, manifest, local commit) and prints the milliseconds.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: Part of the version's mesh data didn't fit the avatar
explanations.summary: The version's meshes are skinned to bones that MCB looks up on your avatar by path, then by name. Some are missing, renamed, or share their name with another object (a merged clothing armature, for example), so a mesh may deform incorrectly or a bone keeps its old position.
fixes: Read the bone or renderer named in the message and check it exists once, with its original name, under the avatar's armature.
Undo armature changes made by other tools, then click Reset to Original Avatar and apply the version again.

explanations.title: Native mesh step
explanations.summary: MCB reports what it did with a version's native meshes: the pose captured when building a version, the size of the built payload, and how many bones and objects it posed when applying one.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: Step of applying or resetting a version
explanations.summary: MCB reports each step of applying, resetting or detecting a version: FBX patches and imports, the avatar definition, sliders, custom veins, blendshape values and the original pose.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: MCB's cache of FBX hashes and version lists
explanations.summary: To avoid re-reading large FBX files and asking the server again, MCB caches each FBX's hash (until the file changes) and the version lists it received, in its folder in Unity's preferences. These lines report hits, saves and clean-ups.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.
If the versions shown look outdated, Advanced Options › Flush Version Caches clears this cache.

explanations.title: MCB fingerprints your FBX files
explanations.summary: MCB computes a hash of your avatar's FBX and of its .originalbase copy to tell which version is applied. It reuses the cached hash until the file changes.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: MCB background task
explanations.summary: MCB runs network and file work, such as fetching the versions of a custom base, as background tasks and reports when each starts, ends and is cleaned up.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: MCB checks or creates a folder
explanations.summary: MCB makes sure a folder it needs exists (its data folder in Unity's preferences, or Assets/MCB for downloaded and built versions) and creates it when missing.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: MCB inspector status
explanations.summary: The MCB inspector reports what it loaded: the versions cached from your last visit (shown right away), the list the Orbiters server sends afterwards, the avatar's FBX files it detected, or the connection coming back.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: MCB requests the version list
explanations.summary: MCB asks the Orbiters server for the versions of the selected custom base that fit your avatar's FBX.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: MCB restores or installs version files
explanations.summary: MCB reports its file work for versions: restoring the original FBX from its .originalbase copy (skipped when it already matches), importing a version's logic prefab, and building FBX patches when you build a version.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: MCB updates a material for the version
explanations.summary: MCB edits the avatar's materials for the applied version: it sets the custom veins as each body material's detail normal map with its strength, removes them on reset, and unlocks locked shaders it needs to edit.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: Magic Sync with Blender
explanations.summary: MCB reports its Magic Sync link with Blender: sessions saved in the project's Library folder and restored after a script reload or restart, so exports from Blender still arrive, and exports detected and imported.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: MCB looks up custom bases for your avatar
explanations.summary: MCB sends the Orbiters server the FBX files of your avatar to find the custom bases that fit it, and caches their banners and thumbnails locally.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.title: Result of an Advanced Options action
explanations.summary: MCB confirms an action you clicked in Advanced Options, such as clearing the version caches or deleting unused generated meshes.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: MCB progress message
explanations.summary: MCB reports a step of its work on your avatar or account.
fixes: Nothing to do. To hide MCB's step-by-step lines, click Advanced Options at the bottom of the MCB inspector and untick Log in Console.

explanations.pattern: ^\[MCB\] The version switch was (?<how>undone|redone) in the scene, but MCB only keeps the files of the last (?<count>\d+) switches
explanations.title: The version switch was {how}, but its files were not kept
explanations.summary: Undo and Redo bring the avatar back in the scene; MCB also puts back the model files a version switch replaced, but it keeps those files for the last {count} switches only. This switch is older, so the files listed under the message were left as they are and may not match the avatar the scene now shows.
fixes: Apply the version you want again from MCB's Versions card: the files and the avatar then match.
Or reset the avatar from MCB.

explanations.needle: in the scene, but these files could not be restored:
explanations.pattern: ^\[MCB\] The version switch was (?<how>undone|redone) in the scene, but these files could not be restored:
explanations.title: The version switch was {how}, but some files could not be put back
explanations.summary: Undo and Redo bring the avatar back in the scene and MCB puts back the model files the switch replaced. Writing the files listed under the message failed (open in another program, read-only, or a full disk), so they may not match the avatar the scene shows.
fixes: Close programs that may hold the files (Blender, an image editor), then apply the version you want again from MCB's Versions card.
Or reset the avatar from MCB.

explanations.pattern: ^\[FileManager\] Kept '(?<path>.+?)': this version ships a different copy
explanations.title: MCB kept your copy of {path}
explanations.summary: Applying a version installs the files its logic package ships and replaces the ones MCB installed before. This file differs from what this version ships and from every copy MCB installed, so it may hold your own changes: MCB left it as it is.
fixes: If you did not change it, delete it and apply the version again to get the shipped copy.
If you did, nothing to do; compare it with the version's copy when something misbehaves.

explanations.pattern: ^\[BlenderExport\] Removed (?<count>\d+) copies of advanced-mesh Blender exports nothing uses any more \((?<size>[^)]+)\)\.
explanations.title: MCB removed {count} unused copies of Blender exports ({size})
explanations.summary: Imports of Blender's Export for MCB keep a copy of each export for the advanced mesh workflow. Copies that no scene or prefab uses any more went to the Recycle Bin; the ones in use, and those made in this session, stay.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: Logged by ReFit's self-checks
explanations.summary: This ReFit message was logged while ReFit's development checks ran (Tools › Orbiters › ReFit › Run Deterministic Tests, or a benchmark or audit). They work on temporary objects and copies, not on the avatars in your scene, and many checks trigger warnings and errors on purpose to verify how ReFit reacts. Only a '[ReFit Tests] FAIL' line means a check failed.
fixes: Nothing to do unless a '[ReFit Tests] FAIL' error names the check that logged it.

explanations.needle: was not registered into undo system and became dangling during an undo operation
explanations.title: A ReFit test object wasn't registered with Undo
explanations.summary: ReFit's reset check adds an object under the rebuilt armature without Undo, to verify that Reset keeps what you add after a refit. When the check then undoes its own changes, Unity warns that this object was never registered with Undo. It only happens while ReFit's development tests run, on temporary test objects.
fixes: Nothing to do: the test's objects are deleted when it ends.

explanations.title: {missing} of {total} bones were missing when applying the refit
explanations.summary: ReFit computes the fit on hidden copies, then rebuilds the clothing's armature from bones it finds again on the real avatar and clothing, by their place in the hierarchy. Some of those bones were no longer there, so ReFit stopped instead of skinning the mesh to empty bones. Every scene change of this run was undone and nothing was saved.
fixes: Run ReFit again, and don't add, delete or reorder objects in the avatar or the clothing until it finishes.
The 'bones-missing-detail' warning just before this error names the missing bones and where ReFit looked for them.
If it happens again with nothing changed, report it to ReFit's developer with both messages.

explanations.title: The bones ReFit couldn't find when applying the refit
explanations.summary: This lists up to 16 bones that were missing when ReFit rebuilt the clothing's armature: their position in the clothing's bone list, their name, where ReFit looked (Target: the avatar being fitted, Asset: the clothing's own objects, SourceAvatar: the avatar it was made for) and their path as child indexes. It always comes with the 'bones-missing' error, which stopped the refit.
fixes: Look for those bones in the Hierarchy: if one was deleted or moved while ReFit ran, undo that change or run ReFit again.
Then follow the 'bones-missing' error logged right after.

explanations.title: The armature replacement failed and was rolled back
explanations.summary: ReFit couldn't give the clothing its new armature on the avatar, so it undid every scene change of this run and saved no mesh or prefab. The ReFit message logged just before this one says why, usually 'bones-missing' or 'prefab-unpack-failed'.
fixes: Fix what the previous ReFit message names, then run ReFit again.
If the clothing is inside a prefab instance that couldn't be unpacked, unpack it yourself (right-click › Prefab › Unpack Completely) and run ReFit again.

explanations.needle: [ReFit] refit-exception: Unexpected error: Scene application did not produce a valid result
explanations.title: Applying the refit failed (follow-up error)
explanations.summary: Despite 'Unexpected error', this only repeats that applying the result failed because of another ReFit error logged just before it in the same run (for example 'bone-apply-incomplete'). ReFit undid its scene changes and saved nothing.
fixes: Fix the ReFit error logged just before this one, then run ReFit again.

explanations.pattern: refit-exception: Unexpected error(?: during computation| while baking)?: (?<error>[^\r\n]*)
explanations.title: ReFit stopped on an unexpected error
explanations.summary: An error inside ReFit stopped the run. ReFit never applies or saves a partial result, so your scene and files are as they were. The error was: {error}
fixes: Run ReFit again. If the same error comes back, update ReFit and Orbiters Toolkit (VRChat Creator Companion).
Report it to ReFit's developer with the full message and its stack trace.

explanations.title: ReFit needs the avatar the asset was made for
explanations.summary: Fitting clothing from one avatar base to another needs the source avatar: the base the clothing was made for. The refit was started without it, so nothing ran.
fixes: In the ReFit wizard, pick that base at 'Which avatar base was the asset made for ?' (a scene object, prefab or FBX).
If the clothing already fits your avatar and only has to follow body blendshapes, choose 'Make it fit blendshapes' instead: that mode needs no source avatar.
If another tool or a script started the refit, it has to pass the original base as the source avatar.

explanations.title: ReFit was started without a clothing mesh
explanations.summary: The refit request had no asset renderer: the clothing or accessory mesh to fit. This happens when the selected object was deleted before ReFit ran, or when a tool or script starts ReFit without one. Nothing was changed.
fixes: In the ReFit wizard, pick the clothing again (an object with a Skinned Mesh Renderer): press Back, or 'Re-fit another asset' on the result page.
If a tool or script started the refit, check that it passes the clothing's renderer.

explanations.title: The avatar or clothing changed while ReFit was working
explanations.summary: ReFit computes in the background so you can keep using Unity. Before applying, it checks that the avatars and the clothing are exactly as they were. A mesh, pose, object or renderer changed in the meantime, so ReFit discarded the result rather than apply it over your edit.
fixes: Run ReFit again and leave the avatar and the clothing untouched until it finishes.
Anything that moves the avatar's bones in the editor, such as a pose preview, also counts as a change: stop it while ReFit runs.

explanations.title: No body mesh found on the {side} avatar
explanations.summary: ReFit fits clothing to an avatar's body: a Skinned Mesh Renderer named 'Body', or else the skinned mesh with the most vertices. The {side} avatar has no skinned mesh besides the clothing itself.
fixes: Pick the avatar's root object (the one holding its body mesh), not its armature or a single bone.
If the avatar is an FBX from your project files, check that it contains the skinned body mesh.

explanations.title: None of the chosen blendshapes exist on the avatar's body
explanations.summary: The clothing should follow body blendshapes, but none of the requested names is a blendshape of the body mesh ReFit uses on the target avatar, so nothing ran. Each missing name has its own 'blendshape-not-found' warning.
fixes: Pick the blendshapes again at 'Which blendshapes should the asset follow ?' in the ReFit wizard: names are case-sensitive.
Check that the body mesh named in the 'blendshape-not-found' warnings is the avatar's real body.

explanations.pattern: Blendshape '(?<shape>.+)' was not found on the target body '(?<body>.+)'
explanations.title: '{shape}' isn't a blendshape of '{body}'
explanations.summary: The clothing should follow the body blendshape '{shape}', but the target avatar's body mesh '{body}' has no blendshape with that exact name, so ReFit skips it. The other blendshapes are still transferred.
fixes: Check the spelling: blendshape names are case-sensitive.
If '{body}' isn't the avatar's real body, name the real body mesh 'Body' (the name ReFit looks for first) and run ReFit again.

explanations.pattern: tube-geometry-invalid: (?<step>.+?): closed tube starting at group
explanations.title: A closed ring of the clothing would be torn
explanations.summary: ReFit fits closed rings (bracelets, rings, loops, closed cuffs) as one piece so they keep their thickness. Here a ring would fold over, collapse or stretch an edge past 8 times its length (step: {step}), so ReFit rejected the whole result: nothing was applied or saved.
fixes: Check that the source avatar is the base the asset was made for, and that the asset sits on it as authored.

Run ReFit again with Preserve closed tubes unticked (on the summary page: Advanced options › Clearance correction › tick Advanced): rings are then fitted like the rest of the cloth. Check them afterwards.
If the ring still looks wrong, fit that piece by hand or commission a manual refit ('The refit doesn't look right ?' on the wizard's result page).

explanations.title: A closed ring may still clip the body
explanations.summary: ReFit fitted the clothing's closed rings (bracelets, loops, closed cuffs) as one piece, then pushed them out of the shaped body. Some sampled contact points are still {depth} mm short of the wanted gap (step: {step}), so the ring may clip there. The check is sampled, not a full collision test.
fixes: Look at the ring on the avatar with that blendshape at 100.
