If it clips, fit it by hand or commission a manual refit ('The refit doesn't look right ?' on the wizard's result page).

explanations.title: The clothing may still clip the body ({depth} mm short)
explanations.summary: This clothing wasn't made for this avatar base, so after fitting it ReFit pushed it out wherever it sank into the body, or into a garment of its outfit worn under it. Each spot may only move so far, and only as much as the fabric around it can follow without folding, so somewhere it is still {depth} mm short of the gap it should keep. ReFit aims for up to about 1 cm of room here, so a few millimetres short doesn't necessarily mean the cloth is inside the body; the value also comes from sampled points, not a full collision test.
fixes: Look at the refitted clothing from all sides, especially where the two bases differ most (chest, hips, crotch, shoulders).
Check that the source avatar is the base the clothing was made for, and that the clothing didn't sink deep into the body before the refit.
Fix visible clipping by hand, or commission a manual refit ('The refit doesn't look right ?' on the ReFit wizard's result page).

explanations.pattern: surface-coverage-limited: (?<shape>.+) clothing layer: clothing surface support remains (?<depth>[0-9.]+)mm short
explanations.title: With '{shape}', this garment may cross the one under it
explanations.summary: This garment is fitted together with another part of its outfit (a shirt under a jacket, for example). With the body blendshape '{shape}', ReFit keeps it on its own side of that garment, but somewhere it stays {depth} mm short after the limited correction, so the two may cross there. The value comes from sampled points, not a full collision test.
fixes: Set '{shape}' to 100 on the avatar, alone and with the other blendshapes you use, and look where the two garments meet.
Fix visible crossings by hand, or commission a manual refit ('The refit doesn't look right ?' on the ReFit wizard's result page).

explanations.pattern: surface-coverage-limited: (?!different-base coverage: )(?<shape>.+?)(?<! clothing layer): clothing surface support remains (?<depth>[0-9.]+)mm short
explanations.title: With '{shape}', the clothing may clip the body
explanations.summary: ReFit made the clothing follow the body blendshape '{shape}' and pushed it out wherever the shaped body would poke through between its vertices. Somewhere it is still {depth} mm short of the gap it should keep after the limited correction, so it may clip with '{shape}' at full weight or combined with other blendshapes. The value comes from sampled points, not a full collision test: a millimetre or two rarely shows.
fixes: Set '{shape}' to 100 on the avatar, alone and with the other blendshapes you use, and look for skin showing through.
Fix visible clipping by hand, or commission a manual refit ('The refit doesn't look right ?' on the ReFit wizard's result page).

explanations.pattern: no-humanoid-rig: '(?<avatar>.+)' has no humanoid Animator avatar
explanations.title: '{avatar}' has no humanoid rig
explanations.summary: ReFit reads an avatar's humanoid bone mapping from its Animator to match the two bodies, size them and keep left and right apart. '{avatar}' has no valid humanoid Avatar, so ReFit guesses its bones from their names instead. Usual bone names work, but the result may be less reliable.
fixes: Select the avatar's model (FBX) in the Project window, open the Rig tab, set Animation Type to Humanoid and click Apply.
Check that the avatar has an Animator whose Avatar field uses that humanoid avatar.
Names starting with '__', such as '__ReFitTest_SourceA' or '__CoverageLayers', are ReFit's temporary test avatars: nothing to do for them.

explanations.title: No clothing bone matches the source avatar
explanations.summary: None of the clothing's bones has a name ReFit finds on the source avatar's skeleton, so ReFit can't pose the clothing on that body. It assumes the clothing already sits on the source avatar exactly where it should.
fixes: Check that the clothing is placed on the source avatar the way it is meant to be worn.
Check that you picked the right source avatar, and that the clothing's bones use the usual names (Hips, Spine, Chest…).

explanations.title: Only {matched} of {total} clothing bones match the source avatar
explanations.summary: ReFit places the clothing on the source avatar by matching bone names (Hips, Spine, UpperArm.L…). Fewer than half of the clothing's skinned bones matched, so its starting pose may be off and the fit less reliable. Many physics or accessory bones lower this count without harm; differently named main bones are the real problem.
fixes: Check that the source avatar is the base the clothing was made for.
If the clothing's main bones are named very differently from the avatar's, rename them to match and run ReFit again.
If the clothing already sits exactly on the source avatar in the scene, you can go ahead.

explanations.pattern: proportions differ \(score (?<score>[0-9.]+), largest offsets: (?<offsets>.+?)\)\. You can still proceed
explanations.title: The avatars' proportions differ (score {score})
explanations.summary: Once both avatars are scaled to the same size, their humanoid bones sit at different places; the largest differences are {offsets}. This never blocks: when the bodies look alike and the bones were moved on purpose, as on many custom bases, the fit follows the body surface and makes up for it. Very different bodies may need touch-ups.
fixes: Go ahead, then check the result around the bones listed.
Make sure the source avatar is the base the clothing was made for, and that both rigs are Humanoid.

explanations.title: ReFit couldn't compare the avatars' proportions
explanations.summary: Before fitting, ReFit compares where the humanoid bones (hips, spine, arms, legs…) of both avatars sit. It found too few of them, usually because a rig isn't Humanoid, so it skipped that check. The refit still runs; you only lose the proportion warning.
fixes: Set both avatars' models to Humanoid (select the FBX › Rig › Animation Type: Humanoid › Apply) to get the check back.
Nothing else to do if the result looks right.

explanations.title: A progress display failed after the refit finished
explanations.summary: The tool that started ReFit (the wizard, MCB, My Avatar or a script) gave it a progress callback, and that callback threw an error when ReFit reported it was done. ReFit ignores it so the result still reaches the tool; the refit itself isn't affected. The callback's error: {error}
fixes: Nothing to do for the refit. If it keeps happening, report it to the author of the tool that started ReFit.

explanations.title: The refit was cancelled
explanations.summary: ReFit stopped before applying anything because the run was cancelled, usually because the window or tool that started it was closed or cancelled the job. Your scene and files are unchanged.
fixes: Run ReFit again and leave its window open until it finishes.

explanations.title: ReFit checked the clothing against the surface under it
explanations.summary: For {step}, ReFit compared the clothing with points sampled densely on the surface under it and moved the cloth out where that surface would poke through between its vertices. 'maximum coverage correction' is the largest move; 'last support residual' is how far it is still short of the gap it should keep. A 'surface-coverage-limited' warning follows when that stays above 0.5 mm.
fixes: Nothing to do: this reports what ReFit corrected.

explanations.pattern: lifted (?<groups>\d+) groups out of the body by up to (?<lift>[0-9.]+)mm
explanations.title: Clothing sunk into the body was lifted out first
explanations.summary: Clothing made for another avatar base can start partly inside the new body. Before its finer repair, ReFit lifted {groups} vertex groups out of the body, by up to {lift} mm.
fixes: Nothing to do: this reports what ReFit corrected.

explanations.title: ReFit kept the clothing's distance to the skin
explanations.summary: After the {step} step, ReFit restored the gap the clothing had to the skin: it pushed parts out where the body would poke through ('outward') and pulled parts back where they ended up too far from it ('inward'; where the body grew, Tightness sets how close). Counts are vertex groups; 'capped' groups reached the largest correction allowed.
fixes: Nothing to do: this reports what ReFit corrected.

If the clothing clips where groups were capped, refit with a tighter fit, or raise 'Max primary total correction (m)' and 'Max transferred total correction (m)' (on the summary page: Advanced options › Clearance correction › tick Advanced).

explanations.title: Separate small pieces were kept together for '{shape}'
explanations.summary: Pieces of the clothing that aren't connected to its main mesh (lace, straps, trims) can be torn apart when the body blendshape '{shape}' moves only part of them. ReFit moved each group of pieces together so they keep their shape.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.pattern: tube-field: (?<step>.+?): preserved cross-sections of (?<count>\d+) closed tube
explanations.title: Closed rings were fitted as one piece
explanations.summary: ReFit found {count} closed ring(s) in the clothing (bracelets, loops, closed cuffs) and moved each along a smooth centre line, so they keep their thickness instead of turning into spikes or flat ribbons (step: {step}). The contact value is sampled, not a full collision test.
fixes: Nothing to do. To fit rings like the rest of the cloth instead, untick Preserve closed tubes (on the summary page: Advanced options › Clearance correction › tick Advanced).

explanations.title: How long a ReFit step took
explanations.summary: ReFit logs the time each background step of the computation took (building indexes, binding to the body, computing the deformation, transferring each blendshape…), for performance checks.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: Skin weights were set for the refitted clothing
explanations.summary: With the armature replaced, the clothing needs weights for the avatar's bones. The counts say how its vertices got them: 'projected' from the nearest body surface, 'blended' with the clothing's own weights mapped to the new bones, or kept from the clothing (preserved bones, projections from the wrong body part rejected, fallbacks).
fixes: Nothing to do.
If the clothing bends wrongly in poses, try again with 'Transfer skin weights from target' unticked (on the summary page, under Advanced options): it then keeps the clothing's own weights.

explanations.title: ReFit rebuilt the clothing's armature
explanations.summary: With 'Replace armature with target's' on (the default when fitting to another avatar), ReFit gives the clothing a new armature built from the avatar's bones. It keeps the clothing's extra bones, adds small helper objects at the ends of bone chains, renames bones to the avatar's names so armature links find them, refreshes the bind poses, removes the old unused bones and checks the result (a drift of 0 means every bone sits where planned).
fixes: Nothing to do. Ctrl+Z right after the refit, or Reset next to the asset in ReFit's 'Re-fitted assets' list, puts the clothing back as it was.

explanations.title: Components were pointed at the clothing's new bones
explanations.summary: Components on the clothing or the avatar that referenced the clothing's old bones (PhysBones, constraints, contacts, VRCFury Armature Link…) now point to the matching bones of its rebuilt armature, so none is left pointing at a deleted bone. ReFit adds helper objects where a reference had no bone to move to, and can also repair Armature Links left outdated by an earlier refit.
fixes: Nothing to do. A reference ReFit couldn't move is reported as a 'component-bone-references-unresolved' or 'vrcfury-armature-link-unresolved' warning.

explanations.pattern: kept-bones: (?<count>\d+) asset bones have no target equivalent
explanations.title: {count} clothing bones have no match on the avatar and are kept
explanations.summary: These bones of the clothing have no equivalent in the avatar's skeleton (skirt, hood, strings and other physics bones, or props). ReFit keeps them and attaches each chain under the avatar bone matching its closest matched parent. With 'Keep extra bones (physics, props)' on, vertices mostly driven by them keep their original weights.
fixes: Nothing to do when these are physics or extra bones.
If the number looks too high, the clothing's main bones may not be named like the avatar's: rename them to the usual names (Hips, Spine, Chest, UpperArm…) and run ReFit again.

explanations.title: ReFit prepared temporary copies to fit on
explanations.summary: ReFit never fits your objects directly: it works on hidden copies of the avatars and the clothing. These lines describe that preparation: bones linked again on the copies, the clothing's current scene pose used as its starting shape, the source copy scaled to the target's size, trouser legs spread apart, the clothing's own copy ignored when looking for the body. Your scene isn't changed by this step.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: {matched} of {total} clothing bones matched the source avatar
explanations.summary: ReFit matched the clothing's bones to the source avatar's skeleton by name and posed its copy on those bones, so the clothing starts out in the source avatar's pose. Below half, ReFit warns with 'armature-match-weak'.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: ReFit kept the clothing's pose as placed
explanations.summary: Moving the clothing's bones onto the source avatar's joints made it sit farther from the source body (mean and 95th-percentile distances in the message), which happens with extra or moved joints. ReFit kept the pose the clothing has in the scene instead.
fixes: Nothing to do if the clothing sits on the source avatar the way it is meant to be worn.
Otherwise place it on the source avatar correctly and run ReFit again.

explanations.title: The clothing is fitted where it sits on the avatar
explanations.summary: The clothing already sits on the target avatar (you are adding body blendshapes, or refitting clothing that is already on it), so ReFit binds it where it is instead of moving it from the source avatar. The matched bone count only helps sort its vertices by body part.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: '{body}' is used as the {side} avatar's body
explanations.summary: ReFit fits clothing to the avatar's body mesh. No mesh on the {side} avatar is named 'Body', so ReFit took the skinned mesh with the most vertices: '{body}'.
fixes: Check that '{body}' is the avatar's body mesh. If it is, nothing to do.
If it isn't, the clothing is fitted to the wrong mesh: make sure the avatar's body mesh is named 'Body', the name ReFit looks for first, and run ReFit again.

explanations.title: The avatars' proportions match (score {score})
explanations.summary: ReFit compared where the humanoid bones of the source and target avatars sit, once both are scaled to the same size. 0 means identical; ReFit warns above 0.05 unless the tool that started it set another limit.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.pattern: Ignoring (?<other>.+?) scale x(?<otherScale>[0-9.]+) because (?<used>.+?) scale x(?<usedScale>[0-9.]+) is the active
explanations.title: ReFit ignored a size measurement that disagreed
explanations.summary: To give the source avatar's copy the target's size, ReFit measures both avatars: body mesh height first, else hips-to-head, else hand span. The {other} suggested x{otherScale}, far from the x{usedScale} of the {used}, so ReFit ignored it. This is normal when bones sit differently on a custom base or the avatars stand in different poses (A-pose, T-pose).
fixes: Nothing to do if the refitted clothing has the right size.

explanations.title: The refitted mesh was saved
explanations.summary: ReFit saved the new mesh as '{path}' and put it on the clothing in the scene. ReFit's changes are blendshapes on it: the fit ('refit' by default, set to 100) when the mesh was refitted, and one per transferred body blendshape. The original mesh and model files are not modified.
fixes: Nothing to do. Keep this file while the clothing uses it: Ctrl+Z puts the original mesh back in the scene but doesn't delete the file.

explanations.title: A refitted prefab was saved
explanations.summary: The clothing kept its own armature, so ReFit also saved its refitted object as a prefab at '{path}', to reuse it outside this scene.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: No standalone prefab was saved
explanations.summary: ReFit saves a prefab of the refitted clothing only when its own object holds the mesh and all its bones. This one is skinned to bones outside its object (the avatar's, for example), or saving failed for the reason given, so the refitted clothing in the scene and the saved mesh are the result.
fixes: Nothing to do: save the scene, or make a prefab of the whole avatar if you need a reusable copy.

explanations.pattern: Unpacked the prefab instance '(?<prefab>.+)' to allow moving '(?<object>.+)'\.
explanations.title: The prefab instance '{prefab}' was unpacked
explanations.summary: Unity doesn't allow moving objects inside a prefab instance, so ReFit unpacked '{prefab}' in the scene to move '{object}' (to rebuild the clothing's armature or put the clothing under the avatar). That scene object is no longer linked to its prefab: later changes to the prefab won't reach it. The prefab asset itself is unchanged.
fixes: Nothing to do if you don't need that link.
Ctrl+Z right after the refit undoes the whole refit, unpacking included.

explanations.title: '{mesh}' has no skinning, so it's fitted as a rigid mesh
explanations.summary: '{mesh}' has no bones or bone weights ReFit can use. ReFit can still reshape it with a blendshape, but can't attach it to the avatar's bones: it keeps following its parent object only.
fixes: Nothing to do for props that follow one bone by being parented to it.
Clothing that should bend with the body needs skin weights: weight-paint it in Blender and import it again.

explanations.pattern: Using active base blendshape\(s\) '(?<shapes>.+)' as the already-fitted
explanations.title: The existing '{shapes}' fit is used as the starting point
explanations.summary: This clothing was refitted before. ReFit takes its active '{shapes}' blendshape as the fitted shape and builds the new blendshapes on top of it, instead of starting again from the unfitted mesh.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: An earlier transfer of '{shape}' was reused
explanations.summary: The clothing already holds a transfer of '{shape}' computed for the same mesh, avatar and settings, so ReFit reused it instead of computing it again.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.pattern: ^\[ReFit\] (?:debug-session-started: |debug-request: |debug-snapshot: |Removed \d+ debug snapshot session|No debug snapshot objects found|Debug flush removed)
explanations.title: ReFit debug mode output
explanations.summary: ReFit's Debug mode is on (ReFit › Settings › Debug mode). Each refit then leaves step-by-step snapshot copies in the scene, under an object named __ReFit_Debug_Session_<date>_<asset>, and logs its settings and every snapshot. The copies are separate scene objects, not part of your avatar.
fixes: Turn Debug mode off in ReFit's Settings when you don't need it.
Delete the snapshot copies with 'Remove debug objects from scene' in ReFit's Settings.

explanations.title: A ReFit self-check is out of date with ReFit's code
explanations.summary: The check '{test}' failed before testing anything: it calls ReFit's internal code by reflection, and that code's signature changed (another number of parameters, or a renamed member). It says nothing about refits themselves, but the check doesn't guard its feature until it's updated.
fixes: Update the test to the current signature (the stack trace shows the test's line), then run the suite again.

explanations.title: A ReFit self-check failed
explanations.summary: ReFit's development test suite (Tools › Orbiters › ReFit › Run Deterministic Tests) ran the check '{test}' and didn't get the expected result. The exception under the name says what went wrong. Until it's fixed, that ReFit feature may give wrong results in this project; the tests themselves only use temporary objects.
fixes: Read the first lines of the exception: an assertion message names the wrong result, while an error raised inside the test usually means the test and ReFit's code are out of step.
Run the suite again; per-test results and timings are written to Temp/ReFitTests/latest.txt in the project folder.
If you aren't developing ReFit, update ReFit and Orbiters Toolkit, and report failures that remain to ReFit's developer.

explanations.title: ReFit's self-checks found failures
explanations.summary: Tools › Orbiters › ReFit › Run Deterministic Tests finished with failed checks. Each '- name: reason' line is one of them; each also has its own '[ReFit Tests] FAIL' error with the full exception.
fixes: Open the FAIL errors for details; per-test results are in Temp/ReFitTests/latest.txt in the project folder.

explanations.title: A ReFit self-check was skipped
explanations.summary: The check '{test}' didn't run; skipped checks are reported as SKIP, never as PASS. The reason given: {reason}
fixes: Nothing to do in a normal run: checks that change the selection or depend on the open scene only run from their own items under Tools › Orbiters › ReFit, and checks that need licensed test models, VRCFury, the VRChat SDK or the Toolkit's avatar gizmos skip when those are missing.

explanations.title: {failed} ReFit self-checks failed
explanations.summary: ReFit's development test suite finished: {passed} passed, {skipped} skipped and {failed} failed. Each failed check is logged above as a '[ReFit Tests] FAIL' error with its exception.
fixes: Open each FAIL error to see what went wrong.
Per-test results and timings are in Temp/ReFitTests/latest.txt in the project folder.

explanations.title: ReFit test-suite output
explanations.summary: This line comes from ReFit's development tests (Tools › Orbiters › ReFit › Run Deterministic Tests and related checks), which only exist in development copies of ReFit. PASS lines, and a final count with 0 failed, mean the checks succeeded; the other lines are measurements the tests print (distances, timings) to compare versions.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: ReFit progress note
explanations.summary: ReFit logs what each step of a refit did, as '[ReFit] code: details'. This line is informational: anything that needs your attention is logged as a warning or an error.
fixes: Nothing to do.

explanations.title: ReFit warning
explanations.summary: ReFit noticed something during a refit that may make the result less accurate; the text after the code says what. Warnings never stop a refit by themselves.
fixes: Read the message, then check the refitted clothing on the avatar with the blendshapes you use.
If the result doesn't look right, commission a manual refit ('The refit doesn't look right ?' on the ReFit wizard's result page).

explanations.title: ReFit couldn't complete the refit
explanations.summary: ReFit stopped because of the problem in the message. It applies a result only when the whole run succeeds, so the scene was left as it was and no file was saved.
fixes: Fix what the message names, then run ReFit again.
If it looks like a bug, report it to ReFit's developer with the full message.

explanations.title: The blueprint ID belongs to someone else's avatar
explanations.summary: The avatar's Pipeline Manager carries the blueprint ID of an avatar another account uploaded, often because the avatar came from a package that kept its creator's ID. VRChat refuses to update an avatar you don't own, so the upload failed after the whole build.
fixes: Select the avatar root, find the Pipeline Manager component and click Detach to clear the blueprint ID.
Build & Publish again: the avatar is uploaded as a new one (the SDK asks for a name and a thumbnail).
With My Avatar installed and your Orbiters account linked to VRChat, this is checked before the build starts.

explanations.needle: [My Avatar] Build & Publish stopped before the build: the thumbnail waiting
explanations.title: VRChat already has this thumbnail
explanations.summary: The VRChat SDK was about to upload a thumbnail identical to the avatar's current one on VRChat, which VRChat refuses at the end of the upload. My Avatar took the thumbnail out of the upload and stopped Build & Publish before the build, so nothing was lost but a click.
fixes: Click Build & Publish again: the avatar is uploaded with its current thumbnail.

explanations.pattern: ^\[My Avatar\] Menu: (?<items>\d+) items left out of the upload \((?<folders>\d+) folders emptied[^)]*\), (?<icons>\d+) default icons\.
explanations.title: My Avatar's menu clean-up: {items} items left out, {icons} icons added
explanations.summary: At upload, on the build copy only, My Avatar removes the menu items deleted in its menu editor (and the avatar's own menu when “Remove default menu” is on, and the toggles of looks hidden in My Avatar), empties {folders} folders that held only those, and gives {icons} items without an icon Orbiters' default icons. The avatar in the scene is unchanged.
fixes: Nothing to do: edit the menu in My Avatar to change what goes.

explanations.title: My Avatar optimized the upload ({level})
explanations.summary: What My Avatar's optimization changed on the build copy of the avatar: {report}. The avatar in the scene and its assets are unchanged.
fixes: Nothing to do.
To change it, pick another level (or off) in My Avatar's Optimization card; it shows the estimate before you upload.

explanations.needle: [My Avatar] Could not name the accessories:
explanations.pattern: ^\[My Avatar\] Could not name the accessories: (?<reason>[^\r\n]+)
explanations.title: My Avatar could not ask Orbiters for the accessories' names
explanations.summary: My Avatar asks Orbiters for readable names of the accessories it recognises. The request failed ({reason}), so the accessories keep the names of their objects for now; it asks again later.
fixes: Nothing to do: names come back once Orbiters answers (HTTP 502 or 503: the server is restarting).
Check that you are signed in to Orbiters if it keeps failing.

explanations.title: VRChat refused the thumbnail: it already has this exact image
explanations.summary: The upload sends a new thumbnail only when one waits in the SDK panel. VRChat compares it with the image it already stores for the avatar and refuses an identical file, so the upload stopped after the whole build. A thumbnail chosen in the panel stays waiting even after the panel reloads the avatar, so this often comes from one picked earlier, or offered while the panel had cleared the blueprint ID. Nothing was changed on VRChat: the avatar keeps its previous version.
fixes: In the SDK panel, click Discard Changes (under the avatar's details) to drop the waiting thumbnail, then Build & Publish again.
Or take a new thumbnail (in My Avatar or with Select New Thumbnail) so the image differs.
With My Avatar 0.9.5 or later this is caught before the build: update it if the upload still gets this far.

explanations.title: VRChat refused a file it already has
explanations.summary: Before uploading a file (the avatar's thumbnail or its asset bundle), the SDK compares it with the latest version VRChat stores. An identical file is refused, so the upload stopped. For the bundle, it means this exact build was uploaded already.
fixes: If it was the thumbnail: click Discard Changes in the SDK panel, or choose a different image, then Build & Publish again.
If it was the bundle: change something in the avatar (or just build again) so the SDK makes a new build, then upload.

explanations.title: The avatar upload failed
explanations.summary: The VRChat SDK announces the failure with this line; the reason is the error it logs right after (in red, from the same place). The avatar on VRChat is unchanged.
fixes: Open the error just after this line: its explanation says what to fix.
Then Build & Publish again.

explanations.needle: Loaded data for an avatar we do not own
explanations.title: The SDK cleared the avatar's blueprint ID
explanations.summary: When the SDK panel loads an avatar, it asks VRChat for the avatar its blueprint ID points to. When VRChat answers that it belongs to another account, or that it doesn't exist (which can also be a passing VRChat error), the panel removes the ID and treats the avatar as a new one.
fixes: If the avatar is yours, press Ctrl+Z (Undo “Cleared the blueprint ID we do not own”) to get the ID back before uploading, or the upload creates a second avatar.
If it isn't yours: fill in the new avatar's name and thumbnail in the SDK panel, then Build & Publish.

explanations.needle: The object of type 'VRCAvatarDescriptor' has been destroyed
explanations.title: The VRChat SDK panel still points to a deleted avatar
explanations.summary: The SDK panel's Builder tab was showing an avatar that no longer exists: a build or test copy, or an avatar you deleted. Something asks the panel for that avatar on every editor update, so the error repeats very fast. Your project is not damaged.
fixes: Select another avatar in the Builder tab of the VRChat SDK panel, or close and reopen the panel.
If My Avatar appears in the stack trace, update it to 0.9.1 or newer: it no longer asks the panel on every update.
Clear the log once it stops: millions of repeats slow Unity's own Console down.

explanations.title: The humanoid rig is missing spine bones
explanations.summary: VRChat needs a humanoid avatar with a full chain from Hips through Spine and Chest to Neck and Head. The model's humanoid mapping leaves some of them out.
fixes: Select the avatar's model (the FBX), open Rig › Configure… and map the missing bones (often Chest or Upper Chest).
Apply, then select the avatar again in the VRChat SDK panel.

explanations.pattern: (?i)blueprint ?id.*(belong|another user|not own|not found|doesn't exist|does not exist|invalid)
explanations.title: The avatar's blueprint ID can't be used
explanations.summary: The blueprint ID on the avatar's Pipeline Manager belongs to another account or to an avatar that no longer exists, so the SDK can't update it.
fixes: Select the avatar root, find the Pipeline Manager component and click Detach to clear the blueprint ID.
Upload again: the avatar is published as a new one.

explanations.title: The avatar is too big once loaded
explanations.summary: VRChat limits how much memory an avatar takes once downloaded and unpacked (textures and meshes count most).
fixes: Lower texture sizes or use crunch/compressed formats (My Avatar's texture optimization does this in one click).
Remove unused meshes and blendshapes, and check accessories you added for very large textures.

explanations.title: The avatar download is too big
explanations.summary: VRChat limits the compressed download size of an avatar.
fixes: Lower texture resolutions and remove unused assets from the avatar.
Accessories and clothes often bring 4K textures: 1K or 2K is usually enough.

explanations.title: VRCFury couldn't finish its build step
explanations.summary: VRCFury applies its toggles, armature links and other features while the avatar builds. One of them failed; the message names the component and object.
fixes: Read the object path in the message: a link target or a toggle often points to an object that was renamed or deleted.
Update VRCFury through the VRChat Creator Companion.
If it started after adding an accessory, remove that accessory's VRCFury components and add it again.

explanations.title: UdonSharp script error
explanations.summary: An UdonSharp script failed to compile or to build its Udon program. UdonSharp only supports part of C#.
fixes: Double-click to open the script at the failing line.
Check that the feature you use is supported by UdonSharp (no generics on your own types, no interfaces, limited LINQ).

explanations.pattern: error CS0246: The type or namespace name '(?<name>[^']+)'
explanations.title: Unknown type or namespace '{name}'
explanations.summary: Code uses '{name}', but no installed package or script defines it. Usually a tool needs another package (VRChat SDK, VRCFury, Newtonsoft JSON…) that is missing or has another version.
fixes: Look at the file path in the message: the package or folder it is in needs '{name}'.
Install or update the missing dependency (VRChat Creator Companion: Manage Project).
If the file is under Assets, an old copy of a tool may clash with its package version: delete the old folder.

explanations.pattern: error CS0234: The type or namespace name '(?<name>[^']+)' does not exist in the namespace '(?<ns>[^']+)'
explanations.title: '{ns}' has no '{name}'
explanations.summary: The installed version of the package that provides '{ns}' doesn't have '{name}'. Two tools expect different versions of it.
fixes: Update both the package named in the file path and the one providing '{ns}'.
If one of them was installed by hand in Assets, remove that copy and install it through the Creator Companion.

explanations.pattern: error CS0101: The namespace '(?<ns>[^']*)' already contains a definition for '(?<name>[^']+)'
explanations.title: '{name}' is defined twice
explanations.summary: The same script exists twice in the project, usually because a tool is installed both in Assets and as a package, or two versions were imported.
fixes: Search the Project window for '{name}' and delete the older copy of the tool (often a folder under Assets).
Old VRChat projects: delete Assets/VRCSDK and Assets/Udon once the SDK is installed as a package.

explanations.pattern: error CS0433: The type '(?<name>[^']+)' exists in both
explanations.title: '{name}' comes from two assemblies
explanations.summary: Two DLLs or assemblies define '{name}'. A library was imported twice by different tools.
fixes: Find the two assemblies named in the message and keep only one (prefer the one installed as a package).

explanations.pattern: error CS1061: '(?<type>[^']+)' does not contain a definition for '(?<member>[^']+)'
explanations.title: '{type}' has no member '{member}'
explanations.summary: Code calls '{member}', which the installed version of '{type}' doesn't have: it was written for another version of a package or of Unity.
fixes: Update the package the file belongs to, and the package that provides '{type}'.

explanations.pattern: error CS0117: '(?<type>[^']+)' does not contain a definition for '(?<member>[^']+)'
explanations.title: '{type}' has no member '{member}'
explanations.summary: Code uses '{member}', which the installed version of '{type}' doesn't have: a package version mismatch.
fixes: Update the package the file belongs to, and the package that provides '{type}'.

explanations.pattern: error CS0103: The name '(?<name>[^']+)' does not exist
explanations.title: '{name}' doesn't exist here
explanations.summary: The code refers to '{name}', which isn't defined: a typo, a removed member, or a missing package.
fixes: Open the file at the line given and check the spelling, or install what defines '{name}'.

explanations.title: Obsolete API in use
explanations.summary: Code uses something marked obsolete. It still works; the tool's author should update it someday.
fixes: Nothing to do unless you wrote this code.

explanations.title: Unused code warning
explanations.summary: The compiler noticed a field or variable that is never used or assigned. It doesn't change how anything works.
fixes: Nothing to do unless you wrote this code.

explanations.title: A package doesn't compile
explanations.summary: Code inside an installed package fails to compile. Usually two packages need different versions of each other, or a package was made for another Unity version.
fixes: Update the package and what it depends on (VRChat Creator Companion: Manage Project).
Check the package supports Unity 2022.3, the version VRChat uses.
While any compile error remains Unity can't enter Play Mode, build or upload, and script changes are not loaded.

explanations.title: Scripts don't compile
explanations.summary: A script has a compile error. While any compile error remains, Unity can't enter Play Mode, build or upload avatars, and recent script changes aren't loaded.
fixes: Double-click the error to open the file at the line.
If the file belongs to a tool, update or reinstall that tool rather than editing it.

explanations.pattern: ^(?<file>[^\r\n(]+)\((?<line>\d+),\d+\): warning (?<code>CS025[23]): Possible unintended reference comparison; to get a value comparison, cast the (?<side>left|right) hand side to type '(?<type>[^']+)'
explanations.title: {code}: compared by reference in {file}
explanations.summary: One side of an == or != has a type that brings its own comparison ({type}), the other side only object or an interface, so C# compares the two references instead. With Unity objects that matters: a destroyed object still compares as not null, because Unity's own null check is skipped.
fixes: Cast the {side} hand side to {type} (line {line}) to compare as that type does, Unity's null check included.
If comparing references is what you want, write ReferenceEquals(a, b) (in tests, Is.SameAs) to say so and silence the warning.
In a package's code, update the package: the warning does not stop it from compiling.

explanations.needle: Multiple precompiled assemblies with the same name
explanations.title: The same DLL is in the project twice ({name})
explanations.summary: Two copies of {name} were found, typically Newtonsoft.Json brought by two tools. Unity loads neither, so everything that depends on it fails.
fixes: Search the project for {name} and delete the older copy, keeping the one the package system provides.
Most VRChat tools use Unity's com.unity.nuget.newtonsoft-json package: copies inside Assets/Plugins can usually go.

explanations.needle: will not be loaded due to errors
explanations.title: A DLL can't be loaded
explanations.summary: {path} depends on another assembly that is missing or has a different version.
fixes: Read the reason under the message, then install or update the assembly it names.

explanations.title: A DLL dependency is missing
explanations.summary: A precompiled assembly refers to '{name}', which isn't in the project or doesn't support the Editor platform.
fixes: Install the package that provides '{name}', or remove the DLL that needs it.

explanations.pattern: The referenced script (?:\((?<script>[^)]*)\) )?on this Behaviour(?: \(Game Object '(?<object>[^']*)'\))? is missing
explanations.title: Missing script on '{object}'
explanations.summary: A component uses a script Unity can't find: the tool it came from isn't installed, its scripts don't compile, or the script's .meta file changed. VRChat may refuse to upload avatars with missing scripts.
fixes: Install the tool the asset was made with (VRCFury, Modular Avatar…); its readme or store page says which.
Fix compile errors first: scripts that don't compile show as missing.
If the tool isn't needed, remove the missing component (Inspector › ⋮ › Remove Component).

explanations.needle: The associated script can not be loaded
explanations.title: A component's script can't be loaded
explanations.summary: The script exists but doesn't compile, so Unity can't use the component.
fixes: Fix the compile errors in red first; this goes away with them.

explanations.needle: has been destroyed but you are still trying to access it
explanations.pattern: The object of type '(?<type>[^']+)' has been destroyed
explanations.title: A destroyed {type} is still used
explanations.summary: Code kept a reference to a {type} after it was deleted (or after a scene change, leaving Play Mode, or a build copy being cleaned up) and used it again.
fixes: If it repeats every frame, the tool holds an outdated reference: close and reopen its window or select something else.
Entering and leaving Play Mode, or reloading the scene, usually clears it.
In your own scripts, check for null first: destroyed Unity objects compare equal to null.

explanations.pattern: The variable (?<field>\S+) of (?<type>\S+) has not been assigned
explanations.title: {type}.{field} is empty
explanations.summary: A field of the {type} component was left empty in the Inspector and its script used it.
fixes: Select the object with the {type} component and fill in {field} in the Inspector.

explanations.pattern: There is no '(?<component>[^']+)' attached to the "(?<object>[^"]+)" game object
explanations.title: '{object}' has no {component}
explanations.summary: A script expected a {component} on '{object}' and didn't find one.
fixes: Add a {component} to '{object}', or check the script looks at the right object.

explanations.title: Something was null
explanations.summary: Code used an object that doesn't exist: an empty field, a missing or deleted object, or something a tool expected to find on your avatar. The first stack frame with a file is where it happened.
fixes: Double-click to open the line that failed.
If it is inside a tool (VRChat SDK, VRCFury…), look at what it was working on: a missing reference or an empty slot on a component is the usual cause.
If it started after updating a tool, update what it depends on too, then restart Unity.

explanations.title: Read past the end of a list
explanations.summary: Code asked for an item past the end of an array or list: usually data shorter than a tool expected (fewer materials, bones or blendshapes).
fixes: Look at the first frame with a file to see what was being read.
If it's a tool, check the object it worked on matches what it expects (same mesh, same armature).

explanations.title: A value was out of range
explanations.summary: Code passed an index or value outside what was allowed, usually a list shorter than expected.
fixes: Look at the first frame with a file to see which value was wrong.

explanations.title: A lookup found nothing
explanations.summary: Code looked something up by name or id and it wasn't there: a renamed object, a missing setting or a stale cache.
fixes: Restart the tool or Unity if it follows a rename or an update.

explanations.title: A list changed while being read
explanations.summary: A tool changed a list while it was looping over it. It's a bug in that tool; trying again usually works.
fixes: Retry the action. If it keeps happening, report it to the tool's author with the stack trace.

explanations.title: A class failed to start
explanations.summary: A class's static setup threw an exception, so the class can't be used until scripts reload. The cause is the inner exception below it.
fixes: Read the inner exception (in the stack trace) and fix that, then let scripts recompile.

explanations.title: Endless recursion
explanations.summary: A method kept calling itself until the stack ran out, often two properties or events triggering each other.
fixes: Look for the same frames repeating in the stack trace: that loop is the cause.

explanations.title: A background task was stopped
explanations.summary: Unity stopped a running thread when scripts reloaded. Harmless.

explanations.needle: can only be called from the main thread
explanations.title: Unity API used from a background thread
explanations.summary: Most Unity functions only work on the main thread. A tool called one from a background task.
fixes: Report it to the tool's author with the stack trace.

explanations.title: A native plugin is missing
explanations.summary: A tool needs a native library (.dll) that is missing, blocked by antivirus, or built for another platform.
fixes: Reinstall the tool. Check your antivirus didn't quarantine the DLL.

explanations.needle: position in a group with only
explanations.title: Editor layout glitch
explanations.summary: An editor window drew a different number of controls between two passes, usually because something changed while it was drawing. It is a display bug of that window.
fixes: Ignore it if it happens once.
If a window keeps repeating it, close and reopen that window or reset the layout (Window › Layouts › Default).

explanations.title: Editor layout error (follow-up)
explanations.summary: An editor window stopped drawing halfway, usually because an earlier error interrupted it. The real cause is the error just before this one.
fixes: Look at the error logged just before this one.

explanations.needle: You are pushing more GUIClips than you are popping
explanations.title: Editor layout error (follow-up)
explanations.summary: An editor window stopped drawing halfway, usually because an earlier error interrupted it. The real cause is the error just before this one.
fixes: Look at the error logged just before this one.

explanations.title: Editor layout error (follow-up)
explanations.summary: An editor window stopped drawing halfway, usually because an earlier error interrupted it.
fixes: Look at the error logged just before this one.

explanations.title: Editor drawing interrupted on purpose
explanations.summary: Unity uses this exception to stop drawing a window after a dialog or a change. Harmless.

explanations.title: Editor style not found
explanations.summary: An editor tool asked for a style that this Unity version doesn't have. Only that window's look is affected.

explanations.title: A saved window belongs to a removed tool
explanations.summary: The window layout refers to a window whose tool was removed or failed to compile.
fixes: Reset the layout (Window › Layouts › Default) if a blank tab stays.

explanations.needle: Layout update is struggling to process current layout
explanations.title: Editor window resizes in a loop
explanations.summary: A UI Toolkit window keeps changing its own size. Only that window is affected.
fixes: Resize or close and reopen the window.

explanations.title: Unity temporary memory notice
explanations.summary: Unity's temporary memory for a frame still held some blocks at the frame's end. Unity then repeats this notice, and lists each leftover block (“Allocation of N bytes at…”), every frame until the blocks are released: about sixty lines per frame, which grows Editor.log by gigabytes and slows every script reload. The project itself is not affected.
fixes: If it started after a script reload and the Mixer console's “Script reloads by package” setting is on, that is the cause: Unity's reload timing diagnostics leak about 100 KB of this memory at every reload in Unity 2022.3. Turn the setting off (Mixer console settings › Timings), then reload scripts once: the leak is gone and the notice stops.

Otherwise, to find what holds the memory, start Unity with the -diag-temp-memory-leak-validation argument (Unity Hub: the project's command line arguments): the notice then shows the call stack of each block, which names the tool or package to fix.

explanations.title: A leftover block of Unity's temporary memory
explanations.summary: One of the blocks Unity's “has unfreed allocations” notice lists, with its size and address. Unity lists them again every frame while they stay held, so the same addresses repeat.
fixes: See the “has unfreed allocations” notice next to it: turning off the Mixer console's “Script reloads by package” setting and reloading scripts clears the common cause, and the -diag-temp-memory-leak-validation argument shows what holds these blocks otherwise.

explanations.title: Unity temporary memory notice
explanations.summary: Unity's job system kept temporary memory longer than expected, typically during heavy editor work. It doesn't affect your project.

explanations.title: Unity internal check failed
explanations.summary: Unity's own code found an unexpected state. Harmless when it happens once; if it repeats or comes with a crash, restart Unity.

explanations.needle: Releasing render texture that is set to be RenderTexture.active
explanations.title: A render texture was released while in use
explanations.summary: A tool (often a thumbnail or preview) released a render texture it was still drawing into. Harmless.

explanations.title: Unity licensing message
explanations.summary: Messages from Unity's license client. Ignore them unless Unity says your license is invalid.

explanations.title: Profiler can't keep up
explanations.summary: The Profiler receives more data than it can process. Only profiling is affected.

explanations.title: Burst couldn't compile a package's jobs
explanations.summary: Burst failed to compile some jobs and falls back to slower code in the editor. Avatar uploads are not affected.
fixes: Restart Unity; update the package named in the message.

explanations.title: Mixed line endings in a script
explanations.summary: The script mixes Windows and Unix line endings. It compiles fine.

explanations.title: Unity runs as administrator
explanations.summary: Files Unity creates as administrator can later be locked for your normal account.
fixes: Start Unity (and the Creator Companion) as your normal user.

explanations.title: An import gave two different results
explanations.summary: Importing the same file twice produced different data. Usually harmless.

explanations.needle: Fallback handler could not load library
explanations.title: Native library lookup
explanations.summary: Mono looked for a native library in several places before finding it. Harmless.

explanations.title: Leftover .meta file
explanations.summary: '{path}.meta' is left from a file or folder that was deleted outside Unity. Unity ignores it.
fixes: Delete the leftover .meta file, or restore the missing file. With Git, check it wasn't left out of a commit.

explanations.needle: but it's in an immutable folder
explanations.title: Package file without a .meta file
explanations.summary: A file inside a package has no .meta file, so Unity ignores it: the package was copied incompletely.
fixes: Reinstall or update the package (VRChat Creator Companion: Manage Project).

explanations.title: Two assets share the same id
explanations.summary: Two files have the same GUID in their .meta files, usually because a folder was duplicated outside Unity. Unity gave '{path}' a new id, so references to it may now point to the other file.
fixes: Check that materials, prefabs and scenes still reference the right asset.
Duplicate assets inside Unity (Ctrl+D) rather than in the file explorer.

explanations.needle: Could not extract GUID in text file
explanations.title: Broken asset file
explanations.summary: A scene, prefab or material file has invalid content, often merge-conflict markers (<<<<<<<) left by Git or a file cut short.
fixes: Open the file in a text editor at the line given and look for <<<<<<< or >>>>>>> markers.
Or restore the file from your last commit or backup (Mixer Git: Log or Backups).

explanations.needle: cannot be extracted by the YAML Parser
explanations.title: Broken asset file
explanations.summary: A Unity text asset can't be read, often because of merge-conflict markers or a file cut short.
fixes: Restore the file from your last commit or backup (Mixer Git: Log or Backups).

explanations.needle: has a different serialization layout when loading
explanations.title: Saved data doesn't match the script
explanations.summary: An asset was saved with another version of a script than the one installed, so Unity skipped part of its data. Common after updating or downgrading the VRChat SDK or a tool.
fixes: Make sure every package has the version the project expects (VRChat Creator Companion: Manage Project).
Reimport the asset (right-click › Reimport); re-save it with the current tools if it persists.

explanations.needle: serialized with a newer version of Unity
explanations.title: Asset from a newer Unity version
explanations.summary: The file was saved by a newer Unity than 2022.3, the version VRChat uses, or it is damaged.
fixes: Get a version of the asset made for Unity 2022.3 from its creator.
Or restore it from a backup.

explanations.title: A prefab reference is broken
explanations.summary: A prefab instance or nested prefab points to a prefab that is no longer in the project.
fixes: Reimport the package the prefab came from.
Or unpack the broken instance (right-click › Prefab › Unpack) and fix it by hand.

explanations.needle: Problem detected while importing the Prefab file
explanations.title: A prefab has problems
explanations.summary: The prefab refers to missing scripts or nested prefabs. The lines below the message list them.
fixes: Install what the prefab needs, or open it and remove the missing parts.

explanations.needle: which resides in a Prefab Asset is disabled
explanations.title: A tool tried to edit a prefab asset directly
explanations.summary: A script tried to move an object inside a prefab asset, which Unity forbids to avoid corrupting it.
fixes: Open the prefab (double-click) before editing it, or report it to the tool's author.

explanations.title: A file can't be imported
explanations.summary: Unity couldn't read the file: it is damaged, locked by another program, or not a format Unity supports.
fixes: Close programs that may lock it (image editors, sync tools) and reimport, or replace the file.

explanations.title: The mesh isn't readable
explanations.summary: A tool needs the vertices of a mesh whose import settings don't keep them in memory.
fixes: Select the model, enable Read/Write in the Model tab of its import settings and click Apply.

explanations.needle: is not readable, the texture memory can not be accessed
explanations.title: The texture isn't readable
explanations.summary: A tool needs the pixels of a texture whose import settings don't keep them in memory.
fixes: Select the texture, enable Read/Write in its import settings and click Apply.

explanations.title: Mesh with broken vertices
explanations.summary: The mesh contains vertices at infinity or NaN, usually from an export problem. It may render wrongly or disappear.
fixes: In Blender: apply transforms, merge by distance and delete loose geometry (Mesh › Clean Up), then export again.

explanations.title: A mesh collider couldn't be built
explanations.summary: The mesh used by a Mesh Collider has no valid triangles for physics (flat or degenerate). The collider does nothing.
fixes: Use a primitive collider, or a simpler mesh for collisions.

explanations.title: Convex collider too detailed
explanations.summary: Convex Mesh Colliders are limited to 255 polygons; Unity simplified it.
fixes: Use a simpler mesh or primitive colliders.

explanations.pattern: doesn't have an? (?:texture|float|color|vector|float or range|integer|int|matrix) property '(?<property>[^']+)'
explanations.title: The material has no '{property}' property
explanations.summary: A script or tool read or set '{property}', which the material's shader doesn't have. Usually it expected another shader; nothing visible changes.
fixes: Nothing to do unless something looks wrong. Otherwise check the material uses the shader the tool expects.

explanations.title: Poiyomi shader doesn't compile
explanations.summary: A Poiyomi shader (often a locked copy) fails to compile; materials using it render pink.
fixes: Unlock the material (Poiyomi/Thry inspector › Unlock), update Poiyomi, then lock it again.
Locked shaders made with an older Poiyomi break after an update: unlock and lock them again.

explanations.title: Shader '{shader}' doesn't compile
explanations.summary: Materials using '{shader}' render pink until it compiles.
fixes: Update the shader package (Poiyomi, lilToon…) to its latest version.
Shaders made for URP or HDRP don't work in VRChat, which uses the built-in render pipeline.

explanations.title: Shader compiler warning
explanations.summary: The shader compiles; the compiler only noted something its author could tidy up.

explanations.needle: Instantiating material due to calling renderer.material during edit mode
explanations.title: A script copied a material in the editor
explanations.summary: A script used renderer.material outside Play Mode, which creates material copies saved into the scene.
fixes: In your own scripts use renderer.sharedMaterial in the editor; otherwise report it to the tool's author.

explanations.needle: Destroying assets is not permitted to avoid data loss
explanations.title: A tool tried to delete an asset
explanations.summary: A script called Destroy on an asset instead of a scene object. Unity refused, so nothing was lost.
fixes: Report it to the tool's author with the stack trace.

explanations.title: More than one Audio Listener
explanations.summary: Several cameras or objects have an Audio Listener, so Unity only uses one. Avatars and test tools often bring their own camera.
fixes: Keep a single Audio Listener in test scenes.

explanations.title: More than one Event System
explanations.summary: Several UI Event Systems are in the scene; only one is used.
fixes: Keep a single Event System in the scene.

explanations.needle: does not support negative scale or size
explanations.title: Collider with negative scale
explanations.summary: A collider is on an object mirrored with a negative scale, which physics doesn't support.
fixes: Use positive scales on objects with colliders; mirror the mesh itself instead.

explanations.needle: Animator is not playing an AnimatorController
explanations.title: The Animator has no controller
explanations.summary: A script talked to an Animator without a controller. On VRChat avatars the controllers are set in the avatar descriptor, so this is normal outside Play Mode testing.

explanations.title: Animator parameter '{param}' doesn't exist
explanations.summary: Something set '{param}', which the current Animator Controller doesn't have (names are case-sensitive).
fixes: Add '{param}' to the controller's parameters or fix its spelling.
On VRChat avatars, check the parameter also exists in the Expression Parameters asset.

explanations.needle: you have used is not valid. Animations will not play
explanations.title: The Animator Controller is invalid
explanations.summary: The controller can't be used, often a layer without a default state or a damaged asset.
fixes: Open the controller and make sure each layer has a default (orange) state.

explanations.needle: Bone length in copied configuration does not match position in animation
explanations.title: Copied humanoid setup doesn't fit
explanations.summary: The model's humanoid Avatar was copied from a model with other proportions. Usually harmless.
fixes: If poses look wrong, set the Rig to Create From This Model instead of copying.

explanations.title: Humanoid mapping points to a missing bone
explanations.summary: The humanoid setup maps a bone the model no longer has (renamed or removed in the FBX).
fixes: Select the model, open Rig › Configure… and map the bones again.

explanations.needle: Look rotation viewing vector is zero
explanations.title: Rotation toward an empty direction
explanations.summary: A script asked an object to look toward its own position. Nothing changes.

explanations.needle: SendMessage cannot be called during Awake, CheckConsistency, or OnValidate
explanations.title: SendMessage during validation
explanations.summary: A component called SendMessage while Unity was validating it. Harmless, and usually from a package rather than your project.

explanations.pattern: The character with Unicode value \\u[0-9A-Fa-f]+ was not found
explanations.title: Missing character in a font
explanations.summary: A TextMesh Pro text uses a character its font asset doesn't have; a fallback or a square is shown.
fixes: Add a fallback font asset that contains the character.

explanations.needle: Non-secure network connections disabled in Player Settings
explanations.title: An http:// request was blocked
explanations.summary: A tool tried to use an http:// address. Unity blocks plain HTTP unless the project allows it, so that request failed.
fixes: The tool should use https:// — report it to its author.
Only if you trust it: Edit › Project Settings › Player › Other Settings › Allow downloads over HTTP.

explanations.title: Network request failed (curl {code})
explanations.summary: Unity or a tool couldn't reach a server: offline, blocked by a firewall, antivirus or proxy, or the server is down. Most tools try again later.
fixes: Check your connection; allow Unity through your firewall or VPN if needed.

explanations.title: No internet connection
explanations.summary: A request couldn't find the server's address: you are offline or DNS is blocked.
fixes: Check your connection and try again.

explanations.title: Server unreachable
explanations.summary: A request couldn't connect: the server is down, or a firewall or VPN blocks it.
fixes: Try again later, or check firewall and VPN settings.

explanations.title: Too many requests
explanations.summary: The server asked to slow down (rate limit).
fixes: Wait a minute before trying again.

explanations.title: Not signed in
explanations.summary: A server refused the request because the session expired or the account isn't signed in.
fixes: Sign in again in the tool (VRChat SDK › Authentication, Orbiters account…).

explanations.title: A file is locked or read-only
explanations.summary: Another program holds the file (OneDrive or Dropbox sync, antivirus, an open preview) or it is read-only.
fixes: Close programs that may use the file and try again.
Keep Unity projects out of synced folders (OneDrive, Desktop, Documents) and exclude them from antivirus scans.

explanations.title: A file is in use by another program
explanations.summary: Another program (sync tool, antivirus, image editor) had the file open while Unity wrote it.
fixes: Close that program and try again; keep the project out of synced folders.

explanations.needle: because it is being used by another process
explanations.title: A file is in use by another program
explanations.summary: Another program had the file open while Unity or a tool needed it.
fixes: Close that program and try again; keep the project out of synced folders.

explanations.title: The file path is too long
explanations.summary: Windows limits paths to 260 characters by default and the project's folders are nested too deep.
fixes: Move the project to a short path, such as C:\Unity\MyAvatar.

explanations.needle: not enough space on the disk
explanations.title: The disk is full
explanations.summary: Unity couldn't write a file because the drive is full. Imports and saves fail until space is freed.
fixes: Free space on the project's drive (the Library folder can be deleted while Unity is closed; it is rebuilt).

explanations.title: Out of memory
explanations.summary: Unity ran out of memory, usually while importing very large textures or meshes.
fixes: Close other programs, lower texture import sizes, and restart Unity.

explanations.title: Out of memory
explanations.summary: A tool tried to allocate more memory than available.
fixes: Restart Unity; if it repeats, the operation (a huge import, a long history) is too big for the memory left.

explanations.title: The graphics card ran out of memory
explanations.summary: Unity couldn't create a texture or buffer on the GPU, usually because video memory is full.
fixes: Close other GPU-heavy programs, lower texture sizes, update your graphics driver.

explanations.needle: An error occurred while resolving packages
explanations.title: Packages couldn't be resolved
explanations.summary: A package listed in Packages/manifest.json can't be found or downloaded.
fixes: Open the project in the VRChat Creator Companion and let it resolve the packages.
Check your internet connection; a package from a repository you removed can't be downloaded.

explanations.title: Unity's diagnostic switches are on
explanations.summary: Some of Unity's diagnostics are switched on (the lines after the message name them). They can slow the editor a little. EnableDomainReloadTimings is the one the Mixer console turns on to measure each package's part of script reloads; the Mixer console hides this notice while it is the only one.
fixes: To turn reload measuring off, untick Script reloads in the Mixer console's settings.
For other switches: Edit › Preferences › Diagnostics, then reset the switches you don't need.

explanations.title: A skinned mesh has a different number of bones than its mesh expects
explanations.summary: A Skinned Mesh Renderer's bone list and its mesh's bind poses must have the same length: one bind pose per bone. They differ here, so Unity can't skin the mesh and draws it unposed (or not at all). It happens when a mesh is put on a renderer made for another skeleton, when bones were removed or the bone list emptied by a tool or a script, or when a mesh made by a script has bind poses but its renderer has no bones yet.
fixes: Click the log's object (or use the Mixer console's context) to find the renderer, then compare its Bones list in the Debug Inspector with the mesh it uses.

Put back the mesh the renderer came with, or re-import the model; a clothing mesh needs the armature it was made for (merge it with VRCFury's Armature Link, Modular Avatar or ReFit rather than reassigning the mesh).
If it only shows while a tool's tests run, nothing to do: the test made the mesh and removes it.

explanations.pattern: ^Main Object Name '(?<name>[^']*)' does not match filename '(?<file>[^']*)'
explanations.title: An asset saved as “{file}” holds an object named “{name}”
explanations.summary: Unity expects the main object of an asset file to carry the file's name. A tool or a script saved an asset whose object has another name (or none), and Unity renamed it to match the file when importing it. Nothing is lost.
fixes: Nothing to do: the asset works and now has the file's name.
If you wrote the code that saves it, set the object's name to the file name (without the extension) before saving.

explanations.needle: XR Plug-in Management Warning: Timeout trying to get package list
explanations.title: XR Plug-in Management could not list the packages in time
explanations.summary: XR Plug-in Management asks the Package Manager for the installed packages when the editor starts. The Package Manager was busy (resolving or importing packages), so it gave up waiting. It only affects the XR settings page; VRChat projects don't use it.
fixes: Nothing to do. If you use XR Plug-in Management, open its settings page again once the editor is idle.

explanations.title: Unity found {count} native allocations never freed
explanations.summary: Some code (Unity's or a package's) allocated native memory with Allocator.Persistent (a NativeArray, a NativeList) and never disposed of it before a script reload or the end of Play Mode. The memory is freed when the editor closes. A few are common and harmless; a count that grows on every reload means a package keeps leaking.
fixes: Nothing to do for a handful.
To find who leaks: Preferences > Jobs > Leak Detection Level > Enabled With Stack Trace, then reproduce: the next message has the stack of the allocation.

explanations.pattern: ^\[Mixer\] The autosave of '.+' could not be read:
explanations.title: Mixer could not restore an edit in progress
explanations.summary: Mixer autosaves the edits of each mesh being sculpted or painted under Library/Orbiters/Mixer/autosave and restores them after a script reload. This autosave could not be read (the message ends with the reason), so the edits made since the last commit are not back on that mesh.
fixes: If the mesh still shows the edits, commit them now so they are saved as a mesh asset.
Otherwise redo the lost strokes; the mesh asset itself was never changed.

explanations.needle: was showing a Mixer working mesh no session shows
explanations.title: Mixer put a renderer's own mesh back
explanations.summary: An Undo or Redo brought back a step recorded while this renderer was being edited in Mixer, which pointed it at Mixer's working copy (a mesh that is never saved) although no session shows it any more. Mixer noticed and put the original mesh back.
fixes: Nothing to do: the renderer shows its own mesh. Press Edit in Mixer to work on it again.

explanations.title: Mixer could not read a mesh's vertex groups
explanations.summary: The vertex groups of a committed mesh are kept beside it in a <mesh>.mixer.json file. This one could not be read (the message ends with the reason), so the mesh opens without its groups.
fixes: Fix or delete the .mixer.json file next to the mesh asset; the groups can be painted again in Mixer's Weights mode.
If the file was edited by hand, check that it is valid JSON.

explanations.needle: [Mixer] Couldn't put the Mixer Hierarchy in the Hierarchy's place
explanations.title: The Mixer Hierarchy could not take Unity's place
explanations.summary: Mixer docks its Hierarchy window where Unity's Hierarchy is through Unity's internal dock API; this Unity build or layout did not let it, so Unity's Hierarchy stays open. Mixer tries again at each reload.
fixes: Open Tools > Orbiters > Mixer Hierarchy and dock it yourself.
Turn off the Replace Unity's Hierarchy option in the Mixer Hierarchy's menu to stop the attempts.

explanations.needle: [Mixer] The Blender link could not listen:
explanations.title: Mixer's Blender link could not open its port
explanations.summary: Mixer listens on a local TCP port for the Mixer extension of Blender and writes the port in an endpoint file under %LOCALAPPDATA%/Orbiters/Mixer. Opening the port failed (the message ends with the reason: a firewall rule, no free port, or the loopback interface refused), so Blender cannot connect to this editor.
fixes: Allow Unity on the loopback interface in the firewall, or free the ports, then switch the link off and on in Mixer's Blender pill.
Sculpting, weights and the other Mixer tools work without the link.

explanations.needle: could not be updated in place: the commit of
explanations.pattern: ^\[Mixer\] '(?<path>.+?)' could not be updated in place: the commit of (?<mesh>.+?) goes to a file of its own\.
explanations.title: Mixer saved {mesh}'s commit in a new file
explanations.summary: Mixer updates a mesh it saved before in place, so everything pointing at it follows. After writing {path}, the file did not hold the edits (Unity kept its old data: the file is read-only, locked by version control, or changed by an importer), so the commit went to a new mesh asset and the renderer now uses it. The old file is as it was.
fixes: Nothing to do: the edits are saved and shown.
Delete the old file if nothing else uses it (the Mixer Project window's target button shows where it is used).
If it happens every time, check the file is not read-only or locked, then update Orbiters Toolkit.

explanations.needle: Mixer: the splats Orbiters - N4N0 sent could not be imported:
explanations.pattern: ^Mixer: the splats Orbiters - N4N0 sent could not be imported: (?<reason>[^\r\n]+)
explanations.title: Mixer could not import the splats Orbiters - N4N0 sent
explanations.summary: Orbiters - N4N0's “Send to Mixer” left a request for this editor, pointing at a session folder whose reconstruction/splats.ply Mixer imports. That failed: {reason}
fixes: “No splats at”: the session folder or its reconstruction is missing (moved, deleted, or the reconstruction did not finish). Finish or open the session in Orbiters - N4N0 and send it again.
If the file exists, make sure nothing else has it open and that the disk is not full, then send it again.

explanations.title: A test set LogAssert.ignoreFailingMessages to {state}
explanations.summary: Unity's test framework notes when a test sets LogAssert.ignoreFailingMessages: while it is true, errors logged during that test don't fail it. It comes from a test that expects errors from outside its own code.
fixes: Nothing to do.
